summary: In this project, an alias is a nonzero lattice momentum at which a quantum walk's one-step symbol exactly equals its value at the origin, so the walk hosts an unwanted duplicate of the intended Dirac point at quasienergy zero or pi.
explanation: Film a spinning wheel with too slow a camera and it can look frozen: fast motion masquerades as none, because coarse sampling cannot tell certain frequencies apart. Lattice models suffer the same disease in space and time. In the project's tested 3+1 quantum-walk regulator, three even-parity corner momenta reproduce the origin's massless point exactly at quasienergy zero, and body-center modes appear at quasienergy pi; each is an alias, a spurious extra particle species. A kernel-checked no-go theorem shows that no momentum-independent onsite coin (a fixed internal rotation applied identically at every site) removes the tested aliases, so escaping them requires changing the walk family itself. Aliasing is the discrete-time cousin of the fermion-doubling problem, with pi-quasienergy copies that only periodic-in-time (Floquet) systems can have.
why: Aliases are this program's version of fermion doubling: any claim that a finite walk regulates a single Dirac fermion must first pass the alias census. The classified alias family plus the all-coins no-go is one of the manuscript's central kernel-checked negative results, steering the search toward genuinely different 3+1 constructions.
example: In the tested successive-axis 3+1 walk, the zero-quasienergy points are the origin plus three even-parity corner aliases (for example a (pi, pi, 0)-type corner), with additional body-center modes at quasienergy pi; the manuscript's interior census also pins exact fully off-axis aliases.
conventions: Program usage (this repo's null-edge manuscript): alias means exact equality of the walk symbol, not approximate near-degeneracy; the zero/pi label refers to quasienergy, the periodic energy of a discrete-time system; and the classification is scoped to the tested successive-axis 3+1 extension and its coin family, not to all conceivable walks.

summary: In this project, a kernel-checked table showing that raw element products of the octonion colour ladder operators swap the roles of squares and idempotents relative to the Fock picture, proving the faithful ladder algebra must use composition of left-multiplication maps.
explanation: Fermionic ladder operators are supposed to satisfy two hallmarks: each one squares to zero, and certain products act like projectors (idempotents) that mark a vacuum. In Furey-style particle models the ladders are built from octonions, which are not associative, so there are two ways to multiply: take raw element products, or compose the operators 'multiply on the left by x'. The anti-Fock dictionary is a Lean-verified table comparing the two. At the operator level the expected Fock rules hold globally; at the element level the rules come out backwards - squares are nonzero while the would-be projector products vanish, and one relation even forces a generator to zero. The dictionary is a no-go record: element products are an unfaithful shortcut, and the project fixes composition of left-multiplication maps as the real semantics.
why: It settles a genuine ambiguity in the octonion particle-physics literature about which product the ladder algebra means, and it does so with a kernel-checked proof rather than by convention. In this project it locks the composition-operator reading for all downstream colour and weak-force constructions.
example: As a composition operator, hatOmega squares to zero exactly as Fock theory demands; but the element square is omega^2 = -v, nonzero, while the element product of omega with its dagger conjugate vanishes - the opposite pattern - and the element relation even forces the isospin element tau_3 to be zero.
conventions: Products in C tensor O are written with explicit parentheses because octonions are nonassociative. The project uses its own XOR binary-label octonion basis with the Fano orientation of PhysicsSM.Algebra.Octonion.Basic; Furey's formulas must pass through the ConventionBridge module before comparison. The dagger on the ladders is Furey's eq-30 conjugation, not plain complex conjugation.
source_refs: Furey 2018 C tensor H tensor O ladder papers; explicit composition semantics in arXiv 1910.08395

summary: In this project's null-edge program, the aperture is one of the named channels in the guard-pinned decomposition of the squared carrier operator D^2: the slot recording directional disagreement among a history's null legs, conjectured to carry the det P origin of mass.
explanation: The null-edge program builds a finite carrier operator D out of lightlike steps, transports, a chirality grading, and a turn amplitude, then squares it. The square splits into separately checked slots, and the aperture is the first of them: it measures how far the null directions in a history point away from one another. The program slogan is that aperture opens disagreement, closure cancels or redistributes it, turn flips chirality, and soldering measures it. Because mass in the companion paper is exactly a disagreement invariant, the determinant det P of a summed momentum matrix, the registered target is that the aperture slot's abstract total-square identity Q_A = Q(sum over edges of alpha_e) equals that det P mass. As of the v3 draft this identification is open: a target, not a claim.
why: If the identification lands, one kernel-checked operator would house mass (aperture), gauge curvature (closure), and chirality flips (turn) as separated channels of a single square, which is this program's meaning of unification-as-decomposition. It is the flagship open slot of the P1 manuscript's carrier layer.
example: In the program's picture, a two-leg history whose null directions disagree has a nonzero aperture slot and the walk acquires a rest gap; for perfectly aligned collinear legs the aperture vanishes and the excitation stays massless on the light cone.
conventions: Channel naming is fixed program-wide: aperture (A), closure (C), turn (T), soldering (E), as in the phase vector b = (b_A, b_C, b_T, b_E) and the checked identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T under covariantly constant soldering. Claim discipline applies: the aperture-equals-det-P mass identification is a registered open target (grade C) and must never be cited as proved.
notation: Q_A, the aperture slot in 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T

summary: In this project, the Q_A block of the squared null-edge Dirac carrier; kernel-checked to equal the invariant mass of the total null momentum, so the operator-level channel measuring the spread of null directions matches the trusted Plucker mass exactly.
explanation: The program's central operator, the carrier, is a finite Dirac-type operator built from null edges. Squaring it splits the result into graded blocks called channels, like a prism separating light into bands. The aperture channel Q_A is the block measuring how widely the bundle of null directions is opened - picture several laser beams leaving one point: if they are parallel the aperture is zero, and the wider the fan, the bigger Q_A. A kernel-checked identity shows Q_A equals the invariant mass squared of the summed null momentum, the same quantity the trusted Plucker-mass theorem computes from pairwise direction disagreement. So the aperture channel ties the draft operator layer to the project's most solid finite result.
why: It is the program's first Move-2 identification: it anchors the speculative carrier decomposition to a trusted kernel-checked theorem, and it upgrades 'mass from null-direction spread' from a kinematic identity to an operator statement.
example: For two null momenta in opposite directions (a back-to-back photon pair), the total momentum is timelike and Q_A is positive, reproducing the invariant mass of the pair; for a single beam, or several parallel beams, Q_A is zero.
conventions: Project normalization is 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T in the covariantly-constant regime, and 4 D#D = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T + 4 E_# with varying soldering; the factors of 4 are convention. Channel shares are signed, and naming channels after forces is a conjectured dictionary in this project, not established physics.
notation: Q_A; 4 D#D = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T + 4 E_#

summary: A two-sided multiplication action (x|y) z = x z y on an algebra acting on itself; in the Furey-Dixon setup the C tensor H Dirac gamma matrices are bar operators, combining one left and one right multiplication in a single map.
explanation: When an algebra acts on itself, there are three natural moves: multiply on the left (L_x z = x z), multiply on the right (R_y z = z y), or do both at once. The bar operator (x|y) does both: it sends z to x z y, like inserting a word between a fixed prefix and a fixed suffix. In Furey's algebraic particle models, left actions rotate spin, right actions rotate chirality and isospin, and the four Dirac gamma matrices of the complex-quaternion factor are bar operators. Because octonions are not associative, the project's version on complex octonions fixes the order of operations explicitly as (x * z) * y, so 'do both at once' has one unambiguous meaning.
why: Keeping left, right, and two-sided actions separate is what lets one algebra carry spin, chirality, and isospin at the same time without the actions interfering; the project reads this split as the algebraic origin of the weak force acting only on left-handed particles. Bar operators are also how Dirac gamma matrices enter the Dixon-algebra construction.
example: In Furey's Weyl-basis convention, gamma^0 is the bar operator 1|i_1: it sends z to 1 * z * i_1, that is, right multiplication by the quaternion unit i_1. The repo scaffolding defines bar x y z = (x * z) * y on complex octonions with the parenthesization explicit.
conventions: The project defines bar x y z = (x * z) * y with explicit parentheses, since C tensor O is nonassociative and x (z y) can differ from (x z) y. Furey's eq-13 gamma formulas are stated in her quaternion labeling; any transfer to the project's XOR octonion basis must go through the convention bridge, and the metric-signature matrix eta is pinned in the DixonDiracGamma module.
notation: (x|y) z = x z y; bar x y z = (x * z) * y
source_refs: Furey, C tensor H tensor O program, eq. 13 (Dirac gammas as bar operators)

summary: In this project, the negative mass shift Delta = -kappa produced by signed closure in a finite null-edge carrier: a bound composite weighs less than the sum of its parts, and the size of the deficit equals an entanglement measure of the paired modes.
explanation: In ordinary physics a bound state weighs less than its separated pieces - a deuteron is lighter than a free proton plus a free neutron - because binding energy is subtracted from the total. The null-edge program reproduces this sign at the finite level: when the closure block of the carrier square couples two null modes, the lowest mass drops by exactly kappa, so the mass shift is Delta = -kappa, never positive. A kernel-checked companion result gives kappa a meaning: it equals a standard entanglement measure (the concurrence) of the two-mode state times the coupling strength. Binding, in this picture, is not extra glue energy; it is the closure channel reorganizing null-direction disagreement so the whole carries less of it than its visible parts.
why: Getting the correct sign of binding from first principles is a nontrivial consistency check on the claim that mass is null-direction disagreement, and equating the deficit with an entanglement deficit connects mass to quantum information. It closed a pre-registered conjecture (C to M) in the program ledger.
example: The finite analogue of the deuteron: two coupled null modes with closure coupling kappa > 0 have ground mass strictly below the free value by kappa, and kappa = C(rho) * lambda where C(rho) is the concurrence of the two-mode state.
conventions: Sign convention: binding makes Delta negative (a mass deficit); the positive quantity kappa = -Delta is called the binding gain. Closure contributions are signed - no positivity of channel shares is claimed - which is exactly what allows the shift to point downward.

summary: In this project, the invariant Delta = min spec(D#D | P) - det P: the gap between the ground value of the squared null-edge carrier on its physical sector and the free Plucker mass; a finite, negative, closure-controlled quantity billed as the program's first new invariant.
explanation: Take the carrier operator D of a finite null-edge system, square it in the Krein sense to get D#D, restrict to a certified positive (physical) sector, and take the smallest spectral value - the true ground mass squared. Separately compute det P, the determinant of the summed null-momentum matrix, which is the free-particle answer the trusted Plucker-mass theorem assigns to the same null data. The binding energy Delta is the difference. For a genuinely free system the two agree and Delta = 0; interactions acting through the closure channel push the ground value below the free value, making Delta negative - the operator analogue of a bound state weighing less than its parts. The program calls Delta its first new invariant because it is defined by the finite operator itself, not imported from continuum physics.
why: Delta reframes the make-or-break bridge between the operator layer and the kinematic layer: the free part becomes an equality theorem, while Delta isolates everything interactions do. As a quantity with no continuum ancestor, it is the program's concrete candidate for genuinely new output.
example: For the free single-mode witness the bottom of the spectrum equals det P exactly, so Delta = 0; turning on a closure coupling kappa in a two-mode carrier lowers the bottom to det P - kappa, giving Delta = -kappa.
conventions: D# is the Krein adjoint, not the Hilbert adjoint, so D#D is the Krein square; the restriction is to a certified positive sector, without which 'ground mass' is not well defined. det P uses the project's momentum-matrix normalization, P equal to the sum of psi_i psi_i-dagger from the Plucker-mass theorem.
notation: Delta = min spec(D#D | P) - det P

summary: In this project's 3+1 quantum-walk regulator, exact eigenmodes with eigenvalues +1 and -1 at the body-center momentum (pi/2, pi/2, pi/2) that persist for every mass angle, proving the cubic regulator can never open a uniform Floquet gap.
explanation: A discrete-time quantum walk advances in ticks, so its energies (quasienergies) live on a circle, and 'gapped' means no modes sit at the special values 0 and pi. The project's 3+1-dimensional walk regulator was audited at every high-symmetry momentum. At the body-center point of the momentum cube, q_B = (pi/2, pi/2, pi/2) - the analogue of the center atom in a body-centered cubic crystal - the one-step matrix is an involution: applied twice it gives the identity, so its eigenvalues are exactly +1 and -1. Explicit eigenvectors exist for every value of the mass angle, so turning on mass never removes these modes. Kernel-checked, this is a no-go: the current cubic regulator has unremovable interior crossings at quasienergies 0 and pi.
why: It shows the mass coin cannot uniformly gap this regulator - a discrete cousin of the fermion-doubling obstructions of lattice field theory - and it fixes a concrete requirement the successor regulator must meet. Publishing exact obstructions instead of hiding them is part of the project's audit discipline.
example: For every mass angle theta, the vectors v_plus = (-u, 0, 1, 0) and v_minus = (u, 0, 1, 0) with u = cos theta + i sin theta satisfy U(q_B) v_plus = v_plus and U(q_B) v_minus = -v_minus, so quasienergies 0 and pi persist at body center.
conventions: Momentum components are in lattice units on the cubic Brillouin zone; the obstruction is stated for the ordered successive-axis cubic walk U^(4) with the project's mass-coin convention (mass angle theta). In Floquet systems both quasienergy 0 and quasienergy pi count as gap-closing.
notation: q_B = (pi/2, pi/2, pi/2); U^(4)(q_B, theta) v_pm = pm v_pm

summary: In this project, the locked audit rule that a no-doubling claim must inspect every zero branch of det D_+(q) = 0 - real, complex, and high-momentum - recording kernel dimensions, chirality, and Krein behavior, because coefficient-level tests alone cannot rule out spurious modes.
explanation: Lattice versions of the Dirac equation are haunted by doublers: unwanted extra particle modes hiding at large momenta. A tempting shortcut says that if the coefficient vector p(q) of the discrete operator vanishes only at the physical point, there are no doublers. The branch-count protocol is the project's rule that this shortcut is insufficient: the real test is where the determinant of the retarded symbol D_+(q) vanishes, since a matrix built from a nonzero null vector can still fail to be invertible. The protocol demands a walk through every solution branch of det D_+(q) = 0 - including complex momenta and high-momentum real branches - recording the kernel dimension, chirality content, and Krein doubling behavior on each, like an accountant checking every ledger line instead of just the front page.
why: Fermion doubling is the classic failure mode of discrete Dirac operators (the Nielsen-Ninomiya barrier), so an honest discrete program needs a doubling audit that cannot be fooled. In this project the protocol is locked as a convention: no-doubling claims that skip it are treated as unproven.
example: A retarded symbol can have p(q) nonzero at every q except the origin and yet satisfy p(q)^2 = 0 along a whole null branch; there det D_+(q) = 0 admits extra kernel modes that only the determinant-level branch walk detects.
conventions: Locked as an audit rule in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: retardedness rules out only coefficient-zero doublers; determinant-level branches, complex branches, kernel dimensions, chirality, and Krein doubling must all be reported. Fixed flat null frames are acceptable for branch-count audits but not for final relativistic continuum claims.
source_refs: Nielsen-Ninomiya 1981 no-go theorem on lattice fermion doubling

summary: The set Z = {q : det D_+(q) = 0} of momenta where the retarded null-edge symbol becomes singular; in this project it is the first-class object of Gate C, which asks which branch of Z carries the physical particle content.
explanation: For a discrete wave operator, plugging in a momentum q gives a finite matrix D_+(q). At most momenta this matrix is invertible and nothing propagates freely; the interesting places are where its determinant vanishes, because there the matrix has a kernel and wave modes can live. Collecting all such momenta gives the branch locus Z, a zero set in momentum space typically made of several sheets or branches - picture the layered sheets of a folded map. One branch should be the physical particle (the mass shell); the others are candidate doublers or ghosts. The project treats Gate C not as coefficient tweaking but as a selection problem on Z: pick the physical branch line and control the kernel spaces attached to each of its points.
why: Whether a discrete operator describes one particle species or several is entirely a question about the geometry of its branch locus, so Z is where doubling, ghost, and chirality problems become visible. In this project, Gate C release is defined as a branch-line selection and kernel-sheaf problem over Z.
example: For the continuum Dirac operator, Z is exactly the mass shell q^2 = m^2 - one physical branch. A naive lattice discretization adds mirror branches near the zone edge; the Wilson term is the classic device for lifting those extra branches away from zero.
conventions: The symbol audited is the retarded one, D_+(q), per the project's retarded/advanced Krein-double convention; branches at complex momenta and at high real momenta belong to Z and may not be discarded. Fixed flat frames are allowed when computing Z in audits, but final continuum claims need local frame data.

summary: In this project, the unifying template for mass: a quadratic measure of the failure to remain a single free null mode, computed through a map that geometry, representation theory, or gauge covariance forces on you rather than one chosen to fit the answer.
explanation: The program's trusted core says a bundle of light-like momenta has invariant mass exactly when the null directions disagree. The canonical-obstruction idea generalizes this into a template: zero locus, plus canonical map, plus quadratic size. Start from the configurations that would be massless, apply a map that the structure of the theory forces on you - not one picked after seeing the data - and measure the square of what the map produces. The Plucker spread of null directions, the Yukawa mass map from right-handed to left-handed states, the Higgs vacuum acting on gauge directions, and the radial Hessian of the Higgs potential are all instances. The word canonical is load-bearing: a map chosen after the mass is known is mere reparametrization, not explanation.
why: It reframes the project as an obstruction-geometry program: not 'all mass is one formula' but 'all mass mechanisms share one pattern', which keeps the trusted finite theorem honest while organizing the Gate C, electroweak, and Yukawa work. It also supplies the falsifiability test: no canonical map, no explanation.
example: For the W and Z bosons the canonical map sends a gauge direction X to X H_0, its action on the Higgs vacuum; directions that move the vacuum acquire mass from the quadratic size of that motion, while the photon direction satisfies X H_0 = 0 and stays massless.
conventions: A map counts as canonical only if it is forced by geometry, representation theory, gauge covariance, or finite algebra; maps tuned after the fact are excluded by definition. Status labels matter in this project: the finite Plucker case is a kernel-checked identity, the electroweak case a structural theorem given Standard Model inputs, and the QCD case has no clean finite obstruction yet.

summary: In this project's null-edge program, a carrier is a compact region carved out purely from causal order (an Alexandrov interval germ between two events) on which a local operator is read; disjoint closed carriers are the program's stand-in for independent local measurements.
explanation: Imagine a universe described only by which events can influence which other events, with no coordinates or grid. To read a measurement locally you still need a finite patch of that universe. In this project a carrier is such a patch built purely from the causal order: roughly, the set of events lying between a past event p and a future event q, called an Alexandrov interval, kept small and compact. Operators are evaluated on carriers, and two measurements count as independent local readings only when their closed carriers do not overlap. Program guardrails warn that overlap-free carriers alone do not guarantee statistical independence, and that a carrier's dimension count must come from structure, not just from how many events it happens to contain.
why: Locality is the whole game for a theory built from causal order alone: without a compact carrier there is no honest notion of a local observable or of independent local random variables. Several program stages (A3c through A3e) were killed precisely for failing carrier-stability and locality gates, so the carrier definition is an active research front, not a settled object.
example: Pick events p and q with p causally before q; the carrier is (a germ of) the set of all events x with p before x and x before q. The draft Lean module AlexandrovNestedGerm.lean proves exact nesting facts about such regions: carrier inclusion, induced-count compatibility, and additive transport of protected-core depth across an endpoint buffer.
conventions: Program rules: carriers must be order-derived and compact; global shell cardinality is rejected as a locality certificate. Locality claims require disjoint closed carriers and averaging over the whole equivariant ensemble rather than one automorphism-breaking packing. A rank-four carrier subspace obtained from cardinality alone licenses a probe tetrad as bookkeeping, not a proof that physical carriers exist.

summary: In this project, one of four graded blocks of the squared null-edge carrier, 4 D#D = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T + 4 E_# - aperture, closure, turn, and a soldering-variation block - conjectured to be finite avatars of the four fundamental forces.
explanation: Squaring the carrier - the finite Dirac-type operator built on null edges - does not give one undifferentiated blob; a kernel-checked identity splits it into four graded blocks, the way a prism splits white light into bands. Each block is called a channel: aperture (Q_A) measures the spread of null directions, closure (Q_C) records signed loop memory, turn (Q_T) counts direction reversals, and the fourth block (E_#) appears when the soldering data comparing directions at neighboring sites varies from site to site. Every contribution to mass squared is accounted to exactly one channel, so the four shares form a budget summing to the whole. The project slogan is that unification is decomposition, not identification: one operator, four separated channels.
why: The channel split turns 'where does mass come from?' into a bookkeeping question with an exact finite answer, and it hosts the program's boldest conjecture: that the four channels are finite avatars of gravity and the three matter forces. That naming dictionary is explicitly conjectural (grade C) in the project ledger, not established physics.
example: The on-shell 3-4-5 checkerboard witness has channel tuple (64, 0, 64, 0) with total 128: the aperture and turn channels each carry half the mass budget, while the closure and soldering-variation channels carry none.
conventions: Normalization: 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T in the covariantly-constant regime and 4 D#D = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T + 4 E_# with varying soldering; the factors of 4 are project convention. E_# is the Krein cross block and is not definitionally the soldering-gradient slot E. Channel shares are signed - no positivity is claimed - and the channel-to-force names are a conjectured dictionary.
notation: Q_A, Q_C, Q_T, E_#; 4 D#D = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T + 4 E_#

summary: In this project, the exact splitting of the squared null-edge carrier operator into named blocks (aperture, closure, turn, solder) that separate the different ways mass can arise; the split is not unique, and classifying that freedom is Paper F's moduli problem.
explanation: Take the project's finite Dirac-like carrier operator D built from null edges and square it. The result splits, exactly and kernel-checked, into named channels: an aperture block measuring directional disagreement, a signed closure block carrying loop effects, a turn block from the mass coin, and a solder-gradient block when the soldering varies. Think of pulling one engine apart into labeled subassemblies: the total is fixed, but where you draw the boundaries between parts is partly a choice. The project slogan is that unification is decomposition, not identification: one operator contains all the channels. Because different labelings can reproduce the same total square, the decomposition has a whole space of alternatives, and Paper F asks which extra structure, if any, selects a preferred one, or proves none can.
why: The four channels are the program's candidate finite avatars of kinetic, gauge, Yukawa, and gravity terms, so the decomposition is where the physics reading enters. Its non-uniqueness is an honesty constraint: any claim hung on a particular channel must survive the moduli problem.
example: The guard-pinned identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T holds in the covariantly-constant regime; with varying soldering it extends to 4 D^#D = Q_A^# + Q_C^# + 4 Q_T + 4 E_#, adding the soldering-gradient (gravity-shaped) block E_#.
conventions: Channel normalization follows the guard-pinned Weitzenbock identity with the displayed factors of 4; channels are signed, with no blockwise positivity claimed. The names aperture, closure, turn, solder are project coinages, and other decompositions of the same square exist - that residual freedom is exactly the moduli problem.

summary: The Feynman checkerboard is a 1+1 dimensional model in which an electron zigzags at light speed on lattice diagonals, paying a small amplitude per direction flip, and the sum over paths provably reproduces the continuum Dirac equation, with mass as the flip rate.
explanation: In Feynman's checkerboard model, an electron in one space and one time dimension moves only along lattice diagonals, always at light speed, going left or right. At each step it may keep its direction or flip, and each flip costs a small amplitude proportional to the mass. Summing the amplitudes over all zigzag paths reproduces the exact propagator of the 1+1 dimensional Dirac equation in the continuum limit. Mass is literally the rate of flipping between the left-moving and right-moving states. In this project the checkerboard matters because it is the one place where a continuum reduction from a lightlike lattice model is actually proven, so the bridge from the project's finite null-edge operators to the checkerboard earns disproportionate effort.
why: It is the cleanest known demonstration that a lightlike discrete substrate can produce a massive relativistic particle, which is exactly the shape of this program's core claim. Because its continuum reduction is proven, the checkerboard bridge anchors the project's discipline about which reductions are theorems and which are still targets.
example: The null-step transfer matrix U_a(k) = exp(-i k a sigma_z) exp(-i mu a sigma_x) has quasienergy cos(omega a) = cos(k a) cos(mu a); expanding for small lattice spacing a gives omega^2 = k^2 + mu^2, the relativistic mass shell.
conventions: The proven reduction is strictly 1+1 dimensional; naive higher-dimensional checkerboards are a recognized obstruction, which this project attacks along a separate anomalous-Floquet route. The project imports the standard checkerboard dispersion with an explicit [import] tag and fixes its own corner-amplitude conventions in the Lean checkerboard modules.
source_refs: Feynman and Hibbs 1965, Quantum Mechanics and Path Integrals, problem 2-6

summary: In this project, the loop or holonomy channel of null-coherence change: a signed contribution recording the memory of going around closed paths, able to cancel directional disagreement and so bind composites, and the program's candidate finite avatar of gauge curvature.
explanation: The program organizes how a bundle of null edges can change its shared coherence into four canonical channels, and closure is the loop one. Imagine walking around a small closed circuit and finding you do not come back exactly the same: the leftover twist is loop memory, called holonomy. In this project that memory enters the squared carrier with a sign, unlike the always-nonnegative aperture cost. A signed term can subtract: closure can reorganize and cancel part of the directional disagreement between edges, which is why it is the program's mechanism for binding composite objects, much as magnetic-like field energy participates in binding in ordinary gauge theory. Read information-theoretically, closure is phase-sensitive loop memory rather than noise, which is precisely what lets it lower a composite's mass.
why: Gauge forces in established physics are curvature, that is, loop holonomy, so closure is where the program hopes Yang-Mills-like structure emerges from finite null data. It also carries the binding story: missing mass in a bound state would be encoded as signed closure plus cross-disagreement.
example: The landed U1HistoryClosureHolonomy result gives finite abelian closure transport: edge holonomy multiplies along a history, is gauge invariant on closed loops, and an exact square loop carries a nontrivial holonomy under a nonidentity gauge.
conventions: Closure is signed by convention: no positivity is claimed for it, and the open physical-sector positivity question lives in this channel. The finite results so far are abelian U(1) holonomy bookkeeping, not a nonabelian Wilson action and not a derivation from the Q_C block.

summary: In this project, the Q_C block of the squared null-edge carrier: the signed, chromomagnetic-style loop term in the guard-pinned identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T, whose positivity on the physical sector is the program's sharpest open crux.
explanation: When the project's finite Dirac-like carrier D is squared, the result decomposes exactly into channels, and Q_C is the block sourced by loops: products of edge terms around closed circuits, analogous to the magnetic-field-squared (in color language, chromomagnetic) piece of a gauge theory's energy. Unlike the aperture block, Q_C is signed: on some states it adds mass-squared, on others it subtracts, which is what would let bound composites be lighter than their parts. The catch is control. The program proves the decomposition identity, but whether the Krein-weighted closure block restricted to the physical positive sector is nonnegative, so no instability hides in the loop term, remains open. A concrete two-by-two witness where the closure share is exactly zero shows the bookkeeping is non-vacuous.
why: If physical-sector closure positivity is proved, the signed mass budget becomes a stability statement and the gauge-curvature reading gains a theorem; if a counterexample appears, the program's binding story must be rebuilt. Repo status notes flag it as the single sharpest open gate in the carrier lane.
example: The signed mass-budget theorem shows the aperture, closure, and turn shares of M^2 = 4 ev(D^2) sum to one; a concrete sigma_x/sigma_z single-edge carrier witness realizes shares (1/2, 0, 1/2), with closure share exactly zero.
conventions: Q_C is normalized by the guard-pinned identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T; the closure share b_C is signed and no positivity is claimed. The target statement is positivity of J Q_C on the physical quotient V'/N, i.e. after applying the Krein metric J, not raw operator positivity.

summary: In this project, the weighted sum C = sum_i w_i n_i of a null bundle's unit sky directions - its total spatial momentum; C = 0 picks out the rest frame of a massive bundle, and a kernel-checked guardrail insists that means at rest, not that no source is present.
explanation: Picture several flashes of light leaving one event, each along a unit direction n_i on the sky and carrying energy weight w_i. Adding the weighted direction arrows gives the closure vector C = sum_i w_i n_i, the bundle's net spatial momentum, while E = sum_i w_i is its total energy. If all directions agree, C has full length E and the bundle is massless, racing along one ray. If the directions disagree, cancellations shorten C, and the shortfall is invariant mass: the repo's draft wrapper proves m^2 = (E^2 - |C|^2) / 4 in its normalization. The name records that C measures how far the direction bundle is from closing up to zero. The guardrail matters because C = 0 is easy to misread: it says the bundle is in its rest frame, not that nothing is there.
why: It turns the relativistic mass formula into pure direction bookkeeping on the celestial sphere, anchoring the program's thesis that mass is null-direction disagreement. The kernel-checked C = 0 guardrail blocks a specific over-claim in the program's P9 source-visibility branch.
example: Two equal flashes in opposite directions have C = 0 and E = 2w: a massive system at rest built entirely from massless constituents, like a sealed box of light that weighs more than the empty box.
conventions: Directions n_i are unit vectors on the celestial sphere and weights w_i are nonnegative energies. The wrapper's angular-variance normalization gives m^2 = (E^2 - |C|^2)/4, a factor of 4 away from the textbook m^2 = E^2 - |P|^2; the manuscript flags naming/convention alignment as still pending. C = 0 is defined as the rest-frame condition, never as absence of a source.

summary: In this project's conjectural information reading, the shared dictionary of null directions that neighboring sites use to compare their data; gravity is read as drift, or failure to globalize, of this directional codebook across the network.
explanation: Suppose every site in a finite network stores information about null directions, like entries written in a local language. For two sites to compare entries they need a shared dictionary saying which local direction corresponds to which - that dictionary is the codebook. As long as one codebook works everywhere, the network behaves like flat, gravity-free space. The program's speculative architecture reads gravity as what happens when no single dictionary can be used globally: the codebook drifts from site to site, and the drift itself becomes dynamical. In the four-channel language, soldering is codebook compatibility between neighbors, and the failure to patch local dictionaries into one global one plays the role curvature plays in general relativity. This is an organizing architecture, explicitly not a theorem derived from the current carrier.
why: It gives the program a single information-theoretic slot for gravity, separated from the three particle-force channels: gravity as dynamics of the directional dictionary itself rather than another field on top. It also sharpens what a future derivation must produce - a codebook drift law.
example: On a flat map every city can share one compass convention, so a single codebook suffices; on a sphere, carrying the direction called north around a loop rotates it, so local direction dictionaries cannot be globally reconciled - that irreconcilability is the gravity-shaped effect.
conventions: No formal definition is pinned in Lean yet; the term is program prose at conjecture grade, and repo documents label the gravity reading as architecture, not theorem. The soldering data of the finite carrier is the intended finite shadow when it is formalized.

summary: In this project's conjectural information reading, a particle: a stable eigen-code of the finite null-information automaton living in a chosen positive sector, so that matter is a protected, self-reproducing pattern of directional information rather than a substance.
explanation: Read the program's finite machinery as an information processor: states carry which-direction data about null edges, a constraint operator quotients out redundancy, and a decoder turns what survives into measurable spectra. A codeword is a state pattern in the chosen positive sector that the dynamics maps back to itself up to phase - a stable eigen-code. The picture comes from error-correcting codes: most bit patterns are noise, but codewords are the special patterns the system protects and carries forward in time. In the program slogan, spacetime, particles, forces, and mass are the decodable geometry, codewords, defects, and compression costs of finite null information. Rank separates massless boundary codewords from massive interior ones, and the continuous mass cost is a spectral area. All of this is architecture at conjecture grade, not landed theorem.
why: It reframes the question of what a particle is as a stability-of-information question the finite program can attack with operator theory. If the reading holds, the particle catalogue becomes a phase catalogue of protected codes, constraining which particles can exist at all.
example: In the finite Hodge witness, e2 is a non-exact positive harmonic class that a commuting Krein-self-adjoint decoder sends to mu^2 e2: a toy codeword with definite mass-squared mu^2.
conventions: A codeword is defined only relative to a chosen J-positive, decoder-invariant subspace; different admissible positive sectors can support different codewords, and no canonical choice is claimed. The particle reading is a project conjecture, not established physics.

summary: In this project, a coin is the small unitary matrix that a quantum-walk-style growth step applies to the internal (spin/frame) state attached to a causal graph; gate D5, coin rigidity, is the formulated claim that little-group covariance essentially fixes the coins.
explanation: Picture a walker on a grid who, before each move, shuffles an internal pointer (like spin up or down) with a small matrix - the coin - and then moves in the direction the pointer says. In this project spacetime itself is built by sequential growth of a causal graph, and each growth step is decorated with such a coin acting on frame and spin data carried by the graph. In the checkerboard lane the mass coin is not a free dial: it is generated by the complex Plucker coordinate of two null momenta, whose modulus sets the rest energy. Gate D5, coin rigidity, is the formulated but unproven claim that demanding covariance under the little group leaves essentially no freedom in the coins.
why: Coins are where dynamics enters growth models: if coin rigidity holds, the dynamics on a growing causal graph is dictated by symmetry rather than chosen by hand. In this project it is the D5 step of the Gate D program from kinematics to dynamics, and the derived Plucker mass coin is the area-to-Dirac-gap manuscript's headline input.
example: In a 1+1 split-step Dirac quantum walk the coin is a 2x2 rotation whose angle plays the role of mass; the project's manuscript replaces the assigned mass by |z|, the modulus of the Plucker coordinate z = psi wedge phi of two null momentum factors, and machine-checks the dependency chain.
conventions: In this project the mass coin is derived, not assigned: it is the complex Plucker datum of null momentum factors. The 3+1 alias theorem is architecture-scoped: within the successive-axis class, no momentum-independent onsite coin removes the zero/pi quasienergy aliases - a theorem about that class, not a universal no-go. Coin rigidity (D5) is formulated, not proved.
source_refs: Mlodinow-Brun successive-axis discrete-time Dirac quantum walks

summary: In this project, the organizing law X^3 = (area datum) X: the many-spinor rest operator obeys B_w^3 = mu^2 B_w with mu^2 the total pairwise null-spinor area, and the pair interaction generator obeys K(z)^3 = |z|^2 K(z) - one finite shape with the squared datum as coefficient.
explanation: An involution is an operator whose square is the identity; cubic closure is the next-simplest algebraic leash: cubing the operator returns the operator itself, scaled by a fixed number. If X^3 = c X with c > 0, every eigenvalue of X is 0, +sqrt(c), or -sqrt(c), so the whole spectrum is pinned by one datum. In the manuscript, two independently landed theorems share this shape: the odd Hermitian rest operator B_w of arbitrarily many null spinors satisfies B_w^3 = mu^2 B_w, where mu^2 is the complete pairwise area budget, and the even quartic interaction generator K(z) satisfies K(z)^3 = |z|^2 K(z) on its pair block. The coefficient is the point: an explicit control obeys a cubic law with the wrong constant, so the spinor origin of the area datum is load-bearing.
why: It compresses the program's derived operators into one slogan - every operator derived so far is annihilated by X^3 - (area datum) X - and pins rest gaps at plus or minus the square root of the area budget. The manuscript states it as a coincidence of theorem shapes, not a unification: no lemma relates B_w to K(z).
example: For two null spinors, B_z^2 = mu^2 times the identity on the whole space; for n spinors, B_w^2 is mu^2 times a projector of trace exactly four, so the rest gap plus or minus mu always lives on a four-dimensional support.
conventions: The closure constant is fixed by the Lagrange identity: the sum over i < j of |z_ij|^2 equals mu^2, the Gram/area budget. A non-decomposable antisymmetric control satisfies Z Z^dagger Z = 1 Z while its total pairwise area is 2, so quoting the cubic law without the coefficient identification loses the content.

summary: In this project, the operator D that turns constraint-quotiented null information into physical spectra; only its chain-homotopy equivalence class matters, since presentations differing by D' = D + Q R + R Q act identically on the surviving cohomology classes.
explanation: The program stores raw directional data in a big finite vector space, then uses a constraint operator Q with Q^2 = 0 to declare some vectors redundant: physics lives on closed-modulo-exact classes, the cohomology. A decoder is a linear operator D, commuting with Q, that reads those surviving classes and outputs numbers you would measure - masses and spectra. Think of a music file: many byte layouts encode the same song, and the decoder turns bytes into sound; two decoders that render every song identically are the same to a listener. The landed DecoderChainHomotopy theorem makes this exact: if D' = D + QR + RQ for any linear map R, then D' still commutes with Q and induces the same action on cohomology, so physical statements may only use the equivalence class.
why: It relocates physics from one matrix to an equivalence class, protecting the program from mistaking presentation artifacts for predictions. The recorded safe synthesis: observables live on a chosen invariant positive subspace of cohomology and must be unchanged by chain-homotopy changes of decoder presentation.
example: On the positive Hodge witness, D'_mu = D_mu + 2Q is a genuinely different matrix from D_mu but acts identically on the positive non-exact harmonic class e2, sending it to mu^2 e2.
conventions: A physical Hilbert space is extra decoder data: a chosen nonzero D-invariant, J-positive subspace of the Q-cohomology, with maximality natural but existence model-dependent and uniqueness not expected. No canonical positive part of the indefinite Krein space is claimed.
notation: D; D' = D + Q R + R Q

summary: Extra data - local frames, edge holonomies, soldering/Gram scale factors - attached to a bare causal graph; in this project causal order supplies the conformal class of geometry for free, so decorations owe exactly the missing scale, no more and no less.
explanation: A bare causal graph records only which events can influence which - like a subway map with stations and arrows but no distances. A decoration is the added quantitative labeling: local frames (tetrads or spin frames) at vertices, parallel-transport data (holonomies) along edges, and soldering or Gram data carrying lengths and volumes. The project enforces an honesty rule taken from continuum theorems of Malament and Hawking-King-McCarthy: causal order alone already fixes geometry up to local rescaling (the conformal class), so order data gets that half for free, and whatever the decorations add must be exactly the scale or volume factor - no more and no less (Sorkin's slogan: order plus number equals geometry).
why: It keeps emergence claims honest: saying the tetrad emerges would conflate a half that causal order gives for free with a half the decorations owe. A project guardrail follows: never claim a bare graph canonically supplies a tetrad or null frame unless a separate theorem derives it.
example: The finite null-edge object is a graph (V, E) decorated with ell_a(x), alpha^a(x), h_a(x), U_a(x), J_x, Gamma_s, chi_E, and Phi_x, plus compatibility laws - the frame, transport, grading, and mass data that the bare graph does not supply.
conventions: Project guardrails (AGENTS.md, docs/NULLSTRAND.md): universal null frames come from decorated tetrad/spin-frame data unless a theorem derives them from the graph; every emergence claim must state which half of the Malament split it addresses (conformal class from order versus scale from decorations).
source_refs: Malament 1977 causal structure theorem
Hawking-King-McCarthy 1976
Sorkin: order + number = geometry

summary: In this project's NERD lane, the I3 internal clock: free Dirac evolution rotates the determinant line det L of the minimal null split at angular frequency 2m, and a labeled postulate reads proper time as that det-line holonomy divided by 2m.
explanation: A massive particle at rest still has something happening inside it: the Dirac equation makes its internal components swirl at angular frequency 2m (twice the mass, in units where hbar = c = 1), the effect known as zitterbewegung. The program packages that swirl geometrically. Split the spinor space into a minimal pair of null pieces; that split carries a one-dimensional determinant line, det L, like the face of a tiny dial. The theorem-shaped statement is that free Dirac evolution rotates this dial at exactly frequency 2m, and the minimal-split symmetry group factors as U(2) = (SU(2) x U(1))/Z_2, with SU(2) the spin frame and U(1) the clock hand. Reading accumulated dial rotation divided by 2m as elapsed proper time is a labeled postulate, not a theorem.
why: It replaces a failed candidate - the internal clock is provably not the modular flow of the momentum state, which is trivial at rest - with a clock that has genuine theorem content, and it cleanly separates spin (SU(2)) from timekeeping (U(1)). In the project it anchors gate I3 and the planned P2 kinematic-dictionary paper.
example: An electron at rest has its det-line dial turning at 2 m_e, roughly 1.6 x 10^21 radians per second; after the dial accumulates rotation angle theta, the postulate assigns elapsed proper time theta / (2 m_e).
conventions: The frequency is 2m, not m, in natural units hbar = c = 1 - the doubled zitterbewegung frequency of Dirac bilinears. Only the rotation frequency and the U(2) = (SU(2) x U(1))/Z_2 factorization are theorem-shaped; proper time = det-line holonomy / 2m is explicitly a labeled postulate.
source_refs: Schrodinger 1930 zitterbewegung analysis of the free Dirac equation

summary: In this project's lattice-walk audits, the first-order generator a quantum walk must show near zero momentum to approximate Dirac dynamics - Hermitian, unit speed, and involutory (squaring to the identity); stay-put no-gos show doubler removal is bought by giving it up.
explanation: Run a discrete-time quantum walk and zoom in on slowly varying states: the one-step update looks like evolution by some generator, its tangent at momentum zero. For the walk to imitate the Dirac equation, that tangent must match the Dirac operator's local form: a Hermitian combination of anticommuting matrices whose square is the identity, so every excitation moves at unit speed with a clean mass structure. That involutory property is a stiff demand. The manuscript's kernel-checked no-gos show that popular fixes for lattice artifacts collide with it: for the Gupta-Short stay-put family that removes doublers, the tangent generator provably cannot be an involution. The freedom to pause is purchased exactly by bending the unit-speed algebra, so no-doublers and an exact involutory Dirac tangent trade off rather than coexist in that class.
why: It isolates the precise algebraic property at stake in fermion-doubling trade-offs, giving the project sharp kernel-checked boundaries in the search for a strictly local, exactly unitary 3+1 walk with the complete involutory tangent - a problem that remains open in both this program and the published one.
example: The massless 3+1 tangent F_0(n) = n_1 alpha_1 + n_2 alpha_2 + n_3 alpha_3 with mutually anticommuting alpha_j satisfies F_0(n)^2 = identity for every unit direction n: every mode moves at exactly speed one, which is the involutory unit-speed property the no-gos guard.
conventions: Unit speed means one lattice site per tick, and involutory means the tangent squares exactly to the identity; the anticommutation of the alpha and beta generators is load-bearing in the stationary-amplitude no-go. These discrete-time unitary obstructions are logically independent of the action-based Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem.
notation: M with M^2 = 1; F_0(n) = sum_j n_j alpha_j
source_refs: Gupta-Short doubler-free quantum walk family (cited as GuptaShortDoubling in the manuscript)

summary: The Dixon algebra is the 64-dimensional tensor product C (x) H (x) O of the complex numbers, quaternions, and octonions; in this project it hosts the internal charge structure of the division-algebra Standard Model program, with kernel-checked signature bricks.
explanation: Multiply together the three interesting number systems beyond the reals: the complex numbers C (2-dimensional), the quaternions H (4-dimensional, noncommutative), and the octonions O (8-dimensional, nonassociative). The tensor product C (x) H (x) O treats them as independent slots that commute with each other, giving a 2 x 4 x 8 = 64-dimensional algebra called the Dixon algebra. In division-algebra approaches to particle physics each slot gets a job: C handles complexification and charge conjugation, H carries spin and chirality, and O carries colour. In this project the Dixon algebra is the arena for building colour and weak ladder operators, represented in Lean as H-valued elements over C (x) O, with a kernel-checked brick classifying which signatures its generator sets can realize.
why: The Dixon algebra is a leading candidate arena for explaining the Standard Model's charge pattern from division algebras alone. In this project it is where the colour and weak ladder constructions live, and where the kernel has both confirmed structures and refuted overreaching claims (for example the anti-Fock element-level no-go).
example: Furey's weak-ladder units i_1 and i_2 (her eq. 29-30) are quaternion units in the H slot, not octonion units; reading them as e_1 and e_2 lands the ladders in C (x) O instead of C (x) H (x) O and silently corrupts the whole weak sector, the exact trap the project's convention reference exists to prevent.
conventions: The R factor of Dixon's full R (x) C (x) H (x) O is left implicit; the project works with C (x) H (x) O. The quaternion units i_1, i_2, i_3 are a separate family from the octonion units e_1 through e_7 (the costliest documented confusion). The octonion factor uses the repo XOR binary-label basis with the locked Fano orientation, not Baez or Furey conventions.
source_refs: G. M. Dixon, Division Algebras (1994)
Furey arXiv:1806.00612

summary: A doubler is a spurious extra fermion branch of a lattice Dirac operator: an unintended zero of the operator at large lattice momentum that mimics an additional particle species and must be excluded at the determinant level, not just by coefficient zeros.
explanation: Put a wave on a grid and sample it only at grid points: a wave that wiggles rapidly between samples can look identical to a slow one. This aliasing effect haunts lattice versions of the Dirac equation. Besides the intended particle near zero momentum, the lattice operator can vanish again at large lattice momenta, creating extra fermion branches, the doublers, that have no continuum counterpart. A famous no-go theorem (Nielsen-Ninomiya) says you cannot remove them while keeping locality and exact chiral symmetry. In this project the audit rule is strict: showing the operator's coefficients vanish only at the right point is not enough, because the matrix determinant det D(q) can still hit zero elsewhere; branch counting must happen at the determinant level.
why: Doublers are the classic failure mode of lattice fermion constructions and the reason the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem exists. For this project, any claim that the null-edge operator describes exactly one fermion species must survive a determinant-level branch count, and this requirement is locked as a program convention.
example: In one dimension the naive lattice derivative has symbol proportional to sin(q a): it vanishes at q = 0 (the intended fermion) and again at q = pi/a (a doubler). The Wilson term adds a momentum-dependent mass that lifts the extra zero at the cost of breaking chiral symmetry.
conventions: Locked audit rule (AGENTS.md, docs/CONVENTIONS.md): retardedness alone is not a no-doubling proof; it only rules out coefficient-zero doublers. The physical test inspects det D_+(q) = 0, or the corresponding mass-shell condition, over the whole momentum torus; and any physical-sector quotient must re-check that off-shell doublers are not dragged back on-shell.
source_refs: Nielsen and Ninomiya 1981 no-go theorem

summary: In this project's finite Dirac-square bookkeeping, the frame term T_frame = sum_ab C_a [nabla_a, C_b] nabla_b is the leftover piece measuring whether lattice transport commutes with the Clifford frame matrices; it vanishes exactly when the finite tetrad postulate holds.
explanation: Squaring the finite Dirac operator D_N = sum_a C_a nabla_a splits the result into three pieces: a Laplacian-like kinetic part, a curvature part built from commutators, and the frame term T_frame = sum_ab C_a [nabla_a, C_b] nabla_b. The frame term exists because stepping across the lattice with nabla_a can change the Clifford coefficient matrices C_b it moves past. Picture carrying a compass across a map whose grid twists underneath you: extra correction terms appear that have nothing to do with distance or curvature. If transport leaves the frame alone, so that every commutator [nabla_a, C_b] is zero, the frame term vanishes; that condition is the project's finite analogue of the tetrad postulate of general relativity.
why: In continuum geometry the tetrad postulate says the frame field is covariantly constant, and its failure signals torsion-like structure. In this project a surviving frame term must never be hidden: the convention is to classify it as a frame or tetrad defect, a torsion- or nonmetricity-like term, or continuum contamination.
example: In docs/CONVENTIONS.md the finite square reads D_N^2 = K_h + C_diamond + T_frame, and the finite tetrad-postulate target is: if [nabla_a, C_b] = 0 for all a and b, then T_frame = 0.
conventions: Locked project convention: T_frame = sum_ab C_a [nabla_a, C_b] nabla_b, and in the full super-Dirac square D^2 = -K_h - C_diamond - T_frame + Phi_H^2 - i Gamma_s sum_a C_a [nabla_a, Phi_H], so the frame term enters with a minus sign. A surviving T_frame must be classified, not absorbed or silently dropped.

summary: In the null-edge program, a Gate is a named checkpoint that must be proved before the next physics-facing claim: Gates A/B lock signs and gradings, Gate H supplies the internal Furey-style algebra, and Gate C, physical chiral release, is the recognized hard blocker.
explanation: The null-edge program organizes its road to physics claims as a ladder of named checkpoints, like locked doors in a game: each Gate is a precisely stated mathematical condition, and a physics-facing claim is allowed only after its gate is passed with a kernel-checked proof. Gates A and B lock the sign and grading discipline of the squared Dirac operator. Gate H asks the internal, octonion-inspired Furey-style algebra to supply charges and gauge structure. Gate C asks the external lattice operator to release one physical chirality; it splits into C0 (species health, plausibly reachable) and C1 (physical chiral release, still open and mandatory for any Standard-Model-facing claim). Later documents add more gates, such as D for dynamics and L0 for Lorentz-ensemble viability. A firm guardrail: passing one gate never opens another; in particular Gate H does not release Gate C.
why: Gates keep an ambitious, speculative program honest: every headline sentence must map either to a kernel-checked theorem or to an explicitly open named gate. They also give agents and reviewers a shared vocabulary for what is proved versus hoped.
example: Gate C is the program's recognized hard blocker: it is proved that the bare retarded null-edge symbol does not release a single chirality (bare alignment fails), so any release must construct a projected physical operator and pass audits such as ghost-zero safety.
conventions: Gate letters are program-internal labels, not standard physics terminology; when a gate statement conflicts with an earlier NERD document, the v2.1 roadmap (docs/NERD_ROADMAP.md) wins.
notation: Gate A, Gate B, Gate C (split C0/C1), Gate D, Gate H, Gate L0

summary: A ghost zero is a zero of a propagator placed on an unwanted fermion branch so the branch seems to vanish; the project's hard rule, after Golterman and Shamir, is that a gauge-charged branch may only be removed by a true inverse-propagator mass gap, never by such a zero.
explanation: A propagator is the amplitude for a particle to travel between two points, written as a function of momentum; its poles (blow-up points) mark real particle branches. Lattice versions of the Dirac equation typically produce unwanted extra branches called doublers, and a tempting trick is to engineer a zero of the propagator right on an unwanted branch so that it drops out of correlation functions. Such a ghost zero only hides the branch: the states are still there at no energy cost, and if they carry gauge charge the gauge field still talks to them through loops and anomalies. The hard rule adopted by this project, following the lattice chiral gauge analyses of Golterman and Shamir, is that genuine removal requires a true mass gap in the inverse propagator, not a zero pasted onto the propagator.
why: This rule blocks a classic false-victory mode in lattice chiral fermion constructions. In this project it is a mandatory audit clause for any claimed Gate C release: the release checklist explicitly requires no gauge-coupled ghost zeros.
example: If an unwanted mirror branch of the walk operator is multiplied by a factor vanishing on that branch, the free two-point function looks clean, but a gauge-charged mirror mode with no inverse-propagator gap still contributes to anomaly accounting; the project labels that configuration forbidden.
conventions: Project hard rule: no gauge-charged branch may be removed solely by a propagator zero; removal must come from a true inverse-propagator mass gap, and ghost-zero safety is a named clause in the Gate C release template.
source_refs: Golterman and Shamir, lattice chiral gauge theory analyses

summary: HNU is project shorthand for the Higashikawa-Nakagawa-Ueda single-Weyl Floquet schedule, an eight-substep driven lattice walk used as the program's live regulator; the changing-lattice live HNU approximation is kernel-checked to converge to the exact massive Dirac flow.
explanation: HNU abbreviates Higashikawa, Nakagawa, and Ueda, whose periodically driven (Floquet) lattice model realizes a single Weyl mode, something static lattices forbid by fermion-doubling theorems. Their schedule is a fixed cycle of eight simple unitary substeps built from Pauli-matrix spin projectors; iterating the cycle gives a quantum walk. This project reconstructed the schedule independently, fixed an internal sign inconsistency in the paper's compact notation, and formalized the exact endpoint in Lean. It then uses the walk as its live lattice regulator: the finite, well-defined stand-in for continuum fermions. Live HNU means the actual many-step endpoint on lattices whose spacing shrinks step by step, and the kernel-checked capstone theorem shows this changing-lattice approximation converges in L2, after Fourier transport, to the exact massive Dirac evolution.
why: The HNU schedule is the program's anomalous-Floquet escape route around fermion doubling, and its convergence theorems are the bridge from finite, exactly unitary walks to genuine Dirac physics. Several of the repository's largest kernel-checked analysis results live in this lane.
example: The Lean theorem positionTotalErrorLp_norm_tendsto_zero states that for a fixed nonzero mass coordinate z, a mass bound, a fixed time, and componentwise-L2 data, the changing-lattice live HNU approximation converges strongly to the exact massive Dirac flow.
conventions: The source paper's compact substep symbol is internally inconsistent if read with a uniform exponential on both labels; the project's corrected convention ties the exponent sign to the projector label (U_j^+ = P_j^+ e^{-ik} + P_j^- and U_j^- = P_j^- e^{+ik} + P_j^+), with the rightmost factor of a product acting first.
notation: HNU; substeps U_j^pm(k) built from projectors P_j^pm = (sigma_0 pm sigma_j)/2
source_refs: Higashikawa, Nakagawa, Ueda 2019, Floquet chiral magnetic effect, arXiv:1806.06868

summary: In this project, involutive compression restricts a quantum walk to one sector of a reflection-like involution, producing a smaller operator whose exact +1 and -1 eigenmodes pin defect states; it is Paper C's engine for showing winding alone does not classify these modes.
explanation: An involution is an operation that is its own undo, like a mirror reflection: apply it twice and nothing has changed. If a quantum walk's step operator is compatible with such a reflection, the state space splits into a symmetric half and an antisymmetric half, and the walk can be compressed, meaning restricted to one half. Eigenvectors of the compressed step with eigenvalue exactly +1 or -1 are defect modes pinned at walls where the walk's sign field changes. Paper C uses this engine on a spinor-derived walk: across all sixteen sign fields on four sites, whether a compression hosts a +1 or -1 mode depends not just on how much the field winds but on where the walls sit relative to the reflection's fixed sites.
why: This is the engine behind Paper C's headline claim: winding alone does not classify mode pinning, which refutes winding-only protection language for this family of walks. It also supplies exact, kernel-checkable finite fixtures instead of numerical evidence.
example: A same-winding counterexample: two sign fields both turn by 2*pi, but only one compression is self-adjoint, and the other compressed sector has neither a +1 nor a -1 mode, even though the corresponding full walk has both.
conventions: Mode labels follow the walk eigenvalue: a +1 eigenvector is a zero-quasienergy mode and a -1 eigenvector is a pi-quasienergy mode; a compression is only trusted where the compressed operator is proved self-adjoint.

summary: The Malament split is this project's rule for emergence claims: causal order alone already fixes the conformal class of spacetime (light cones and shapes), so added decorations owe exactly the remaining scale factor, and every emergence claim must say which half it delivers.
explanation: A classical theorem of Malament (building on Hawking, King, and McCarthy) says that in a well-behaved spacetime, the causal order, meaning the record of which events can influence which, already determines the geometry up to a local rescaling. In other words, order fixes the conformal class: all light cones and angles, but not sizes. This project turns that theorem into a bookkeeping rule for emergence claims, following Sorkin's slogan that order plus number equals geometry. If you claim spacetime emerges from a causal network, the conformal half comes for free from the ordering, so any decorations you add (edge labels, Gram data, counting measure) owe exactly the missing scale or volume factor, no more and no less. Saying the tetrad emerges without this split conflates a free half with an owed half.
why: The split prevents over-claiming in quantum-gravity-style emergence arguments, where crediting decorations with structure the order already provides makes a construction look deeper than it is. In this repository it is an always-on guardrail written into AGENTS.md.
example: A repo claim that soldering Gram data on null edges yields a tetrad must be stated as two audited halves: the causal order supplies the conformal class, and the Gram decorations supply the scale factor.
conventions: Project labeling rule: every emergence claim must state which half it addresses, the conformal class (free, from causal order) or the scale (owed, from decorations).
source_refs: Malament 1977, J. Math. Phys. 18, 1399
Hawking, King, McCarthy 1976, J. Math. Phys. 17, 174
Sorkin, order plus number equals geometry

summary: In this project, a kernel-checked signed decomposition of squared mass: from the finite identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T, the aperture, closure, and turn shares of M^2 provably sum to one; shares may be negative and no positivity is claimed.
explanation: Think of splitting a restaurant bill three ways: the shares must total one hundred percent, but nothing stops one share from being negative (someone gets refunded). The project's finite Weitzenboeck-style identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T splits the square of the Dirac-type operator into an aperture piece (how spread out the null directions are), a closure piece (how badly they fail to cancel), and a turn piece. Feeding this to any linear expectation ev makes the squared mass M^2 = 4 ev(D^2) inherit three signed shares, and the Lean theorem signed_budget_sum_one proves they sum to exactly one. A concrete 2x2 single-edge carrier witness shows the statement is not vacuous. Positivity of individual shares is deliberately not claimed.
why: It gives an exact accounting language for where mass comes from in the program - spreading, failure to close, turning - and a scaffold for multi-channel phase-diagram work; stating it in signed form keeps the program honest about what is not yet proved (positivity, and whether the channel names are physics).
example: The S6 flagship's 2x2 single-edge carrier witness: an explicit small matrix model in which the aperture, closure, and turn shares are computed and visibly sum to one.
conventions: The channel normalization is the guard-pinned identity 4 D^2 = Q_A + Q_C + 4 Q_T (the turn channel carries the factor 4). Shares are signed; positivity and the physical reading of the channel names are separate open questions in this draft research program.

summary: The mass coin is the internal rotation exp(-i a B_z) that a Dirac quantum walk applies each step to mix its two direction components; in this project it is generated by the Pluecker coordinate z of two null spinors rather than being an independently assigned mass parameter.
explanation: A Dirac quantum walk alternates two moves: a shift that carries each internal component one site left or right at light speed, and a coin, an internal rotation that mixes the two components. The coin that creates mass is exp(-i a B_z), where B_z = [[0, z], [zbar, 0]] is the odd Hermitian matrix built from a complex number z. Writing mu = |z|, the coin equals cos(a mu) Id - i sin(a mu) B_z/mu: diagonal entries keep direction with weight cos(a mu), and off-diagonal entries turn with weight -i sin(a mu) times a phase z/mu or zbar/mu. Standard walks treat mass as a free dial; here z is the Pluecker (wedge) coordinate of two null spinors, so the mass is derived, with rest energy |z| and spectral gap 2|z|.
why: The mass coin realizes the program's central identity, mass from null-direction disagreement, inside an exactly unitary dynamics; the one-parameter group law C_z(a) C_z(b) = C_z(a+b) and the rest spectrum are kernel-checked in Lean.
example: At momentum k the walk symbol is U_a(k; z) = exp(-i a k Gamma) exp(-i a B_z), giving the exact dispersion relation cos(omega a) = cos(k a) cos(mu a); at k = 0 the two eigenphases are exp(-i a mu) and exp(+i a mu).
conventions: The project convention is exp(-i a B_z) with B_z = [[0, z], [zbar, 0]]; opposite turn orientations carry z and zbar; under the opposite checkerboard sign convention the corner parameter tan(a mu) changes sign; the construction derives the operator and its zero locus but selects no absolute mass scale.
notation: exp(-i a B_z), B_z = [[0, z], [zbar, 0]], mu = |z|

summary: In this project, a kernel-checked finite theorem: the pairwise Plucker mass of a merged bundle of null spinors equals the sum of the sub-bundle masses plus all cross-pair disagreement, so combining never decreases mass - mass can be redistributed but not copied.
explanation: Take two bags of arrows, where each arrow is a null 2-spinor. Give each bag a mass by summing, over all pairs inside it, the squared wedge |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2 - a measure of how much the arrows disagree in direction. The kernel-checked theorem pairwiseMass_append says: pour the bags together, and the combined mass is bag one plus bag two plus every cross pair between the bags. The cross terms are nonnegative, so merging never decreases mass (superadditivity), with equality exactly when every cross pair is collinear - two bundles bind only if they disagree. The name echoes entanglement monogamy: the quantity is constrained under combination. It is a finite kinematic identity about the matrix model, not a physical hadron-mass statement.
why: It is one of the new finite theorems in the program's methodology-first all-mass package: a conservation-law shape (mass can be redistributed but not copied) and the exact off-diagonal accounting that any future binding-energy bridge would have to use.
example: Two single-spinor bundles {psi} and {phi} each have pairwise mass zero; their union has mass |psi wedge phi|^2 - mass created purely by the pair's non-collinearity.
conventions: Here mass means the finite pairwise Plucker invariant (sum over pairs i < j of |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2, spinors as Fin 2 -> C); it is not a numeric physical mass and carries no continuum or mass-gap content. The project makes no priority claim over the mature entanglement-monogamy literature.

summary: NERD / NRQG (Null-Edge Relativistic Dynamics / Null-Edge Relational Quantum Geometry) is this repository's research program aiming to derive Dirac fermions, mass, and spacetime structure from finite null-edge data, organized by a gate ladder and claim discipline.
explanation: NERD / NRQG is the umbrella name for the research program this repository serves: the bet that Dirac fermions, mass, gauge structure, and ultimately spacetime geometry can be derived from finite data attached to null (lightlike) edges. The program is written down in four treatises (NERD_1 through NERD_4) plus a dynamics proposal; when documents disagree, the v2.1 revision (NERD_4) wins. Its working parts are a ladder of named gates (checkpoints such as Gate C for chiral release), a claim-label discipline separating theorems from proposals and speculation, and a publication plan. Two structural revisions bind every task: the finite null lattice is only a gauge-fixed regulator, with the intended ontology a Poisson-sprinkled causal order, and the internal clock is the determinant line of the minimal null split.
why: The roadmap exists so that many agents pull from one ladder, one claim discipline, and one track assignment instead of re-deriving them from four source treatises; it is the governing document for what the program may currently claim.
