summary: In this project, null coherence is the agreement of lightlike directions across a bundle of primitives: while all directions share one complex line the total momentum stays massless; particles are stable patterns of this agreement and mass is the invariant residue of its failure.
explanation: Each primitive in the program carries a lightlike direction, recorded as a two-component spinor. A bundle of primitives is null-coherent when all these directions lie along one complex line: then the total momentum matrix stays on the light cone and the bundle is massless. When two distinct directions open up, coherence fails, and the failure is measured by the wedge (Pluecker) area z of the spinor pair: the determinant of the total momentum equals |z|^2, exactly the squared rest scale. The program's organizing bet reads the Standard Model as a phase catalogue of null-coherence carriers: particles are stable coherence patterns (positive-sector eigenmodes), forces are the canonical ways coherence changes (aperture opens disagreement, closure cancels it, turn flips chirality, soldering measures it), and mass is the invariant residue of coherence failure.
why: Null coherence is the candidate ontology under the whole program: it reframes mass as relational geometry, lightlike parts that cannot agree, rather than a substance. Only the finite determinant identity and its operator consequences are machine-verified; the ontology itself is an organizing bet.
example: Two collinear null spinors give z = 0: coherent and massless. Two distinct directions give |z| > 0: the momentum sum moves inside the light cone and the pair carries rest energy |z|.
conventions: Claim-grade convention: null coherence as an ontology carries the project's speculative grade, while the anchoring identity det P_tot = |z|^2 is machine-verified; prose must not promote the former using the latter's verification mark.

summary: In this project, a null edge is a lightlike link of a causal graph, and the core program claim is that primitive spacetime propagation is supported only on such lightlike edges, while internal data such as Higgs values may live on vertices or fibers.
explanation: In this project spacetime is modeled as a graph, and a null edge is a link that is lightlike: its direction has zero spacetime length in the metric, the direction a light ray travels. The program's core ontology claim, a working hypothesis and not established physics, is that all primitive propagation happens along such lightlike edges. Nothing fundamental moves slower than light; slower, massive motion is supposed to emerge from zigzag combinations of lightlike steps, as in the Feynman checkerboard. The claim is deliberately scoped to transport: internal data need not ride on light. Higgs-like values may sit on vertices, gauge transport data on edges, and Yukawa maps on fibers. The null directions ell_a carry the support of the project's finite Dirac operator.
why: It is the founding hypothesis of the NullStrand/NERD program: mass, chirality, and geometry are to be reconstructed from lightlike-only transport. It fixes the operator architecture (null support in the directions ell_a) that all of the repo's finite Dirac results build on.
example: The 1+1 dimensional instance is the Feynman checkerboard: the electron moves only on light-cone diagonals, and mass appears as the amplitude for corner flips between the two lightlike directions.
conventions: The mostly-minus signature is locked, so null means p^2 = 0. The claim scope is locked in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: it concerns primitive transport only, and internal field values need not live on light. The null support directions ell_a must never be identified with the Clifford soldering covectors alpha^a.

summary: A null history is a discrete lattice path that moves at light speed every step; in this project's walk, straight steps carry cos(a mu), opposite turns carry the Pluecker coordinate z and its conjugate zbar, and mass arises entirely from direction changes.
explanation: Put a particle on a line of lattice sites and force it to hop one site per tick at light speed, either left or right; the complete record of hops is a null history, null meaning lightlike. A history that never turns describes free massless motion. Each turn, or corner, costs amplitude: straight steps contribute cos(a mu), and every turn contributes -i sin(a mu) times a unit phase, where turns of one orientation carry z/mu and opposite turns carry zbar/mu, with z the complex Pluecker coordinate and mu = |z|. Summing these amplitudes over all histories reproduces the exactly unitary walk, so mass enters the dynamics only through direction changes. This sharpens Feynman's checkerboard picture: the corner weight is derived from spinor geometry instead of being an assigned mass.
why: Null histories make the slogan that mass is direction change an exact finite statement rather than a heuristic. The directed-edge theorem, kernel-checked in Lean, proves the complete oriented history sum equals the corresponding transfer-matrix power.
example: An n-step history h with c(h) turns has amplitude e^{i Phi_k(h)} cos(a mu)^{n-c(h)} (-i sin(a mu))^{c(h)} Xi_z(h), where Xi_z(h) is a product of unit-modulus orientation factors; the exact z = 3 + 4i control proves the two normalized orientation factors are nonzero and unequal.
conventions: Which turn orientation carries z versus zbar is an orientation convention inherited from the mass coin; under the opposite checkerboard sign convention the corner parameter tan(a mu) changes sign; the separate Gaussian-rational path-sum declaration uses a real mass with corner weight +i epsilon m in its stated convention.
notation: A_a(h) = e^{i Phi_k(h)} cos(a mu)^{n-c(h)} (-i sin(a mu))^{c(h)} Xi_z(h)

summary: In this project: d future-null directions ell_A built from a spatial simplex, plus dual covectors alpha^A with alpha^A(ell_B) = delta^A_B; the frame in which the null-edge Dirac operator differentiates along ell_A but takes its Clifford symbol from alpha^A.
explanation: Picture d arrows in spacetime, each lying on the light cone, whose spatial parts point to the corners of a regular simplex (in four dimensions, a tetrahedron), so they are spread as evenly as possible and sum to a purely timelike total. These are the frame directions ell_A. Null directions are degenerate - each has zero length - so you cannot use them directly to measure components. Instead each ell_A gets a partner covector alpha^A, a linear measuring functional defined so that alpha^A applied to ell_B gives 1 when A equals B and 0 otherwise, exactly like a dual basis. The project's Dirac operator takes finite differences along the null directions but multiplies by Clifford elements built from the duals. The construction works in every dimension d >= 2; it does not single out four dimensions.
why: Trying to solder with the flattened null vectors themselves fails: a sum of null tensor squares is traceless, so it can never reproduce the identity symbol a Dirac operator needs. The dual frame evades this trace obstruction, which makes it the backbone of the program's dual-soldered finite null-edge Dirac algebra.
example: For d = 4, take four unit vectors n_A pointing to the vertices of a tetrahedron with n_A . n_B = -1/3 for A != B and sum_A n_A = 0; then ell_A = (1, n_A) is future null and alpha^A = (1/4) dt + (3/4) n_A . dx satisfies alpha^A(ell_B) = delta^A_B.
conventions: Mostly-minus metric signature. Normalization: n_A . n_A = 1, n_A . n_B = -1/(d-1) for A != B, sum_A n_A = 0, ell_A = (1, n_A), alpha^A(ell_B) = delta^A_B. If null vectors are rescaled, the duals must be rescaled consistently - never mix scaled vectors with unscaled duals. Project rule: the Clifford symbol comes from the dual covectors alpha^a (dual soldering); the diagonal operator sum_a c(ell_a^flat) nabla_ell_a is retired by convention because of the trace obstruction.

summary: In this project's mass construction, the null-spinor area is the modulus |z| of z = psi wedge phi for two null spinors psi, phi in C^2; it equals sqrt(det P_tot) of the summed momentum, gives the rest energy directly, and vanishes exactly when the spinors are collinear.
explanation: A single beam of light is massless, but two beams pointing in different directions, taken together, act like a massive object: their total momentum is timelike. The project encodes each lightlike momentum by a two-component complex spinor. A pair of such spinors (psi, phi) spans a parallelogram in spinor space whose complex area is z = psi wedge phi. By the Cauchy-Binet identity, the determinant of the total momentum matrix equals |z|^2, so the invariant mass of the pair is exactly the area |z|. When the two spinors are parallel - the light directions coincide - the area collapses to zero and the system stays massless. The phase of z is extra orientation data that the total momentum forgets but that directed dynamics and transported comparisons remember.
why: It replaces the assumed mass parameter of a Dirac quantum walk with a derived geometric quantity: mass squared is the area opened between two null directions. In this repo it is the trusted P1 finite kinematic identity anchoring the whole mass-as-quadratic-obstruction program; it is a finite identity, not a claim about nature.
example: psi = (1,0) and phi = (0,1) give z = 1; the total momentum matrix is the identity, det = 1, rest energy 1. psi = (1,0) and phi = (2,0) are collinear: z = 0 and the sum stays lightlike.
conventions: Spinors live in C^2 with P_tot = psi psi^dagger + phi phi^dagger and z = psi wedge phi = psi_1 phi_2 - psi_2 phi_1. The mass operator convention is B_z = [[0, z], [zbar, 0]] relative to the chiral grading Gamma = diag(1, -1); rest energy |z|, spectral band gap 2|z|. Multiplying z by a unit phase conjugates B_z by a unitary, so P_tot fixes only the orbit radius |z|; the oriented null factorization carries the phase. No absolute mass scale is selected.

summary: In this project, the null-strand principle is a conjectured internal axiom: matter fills the exterior algebra of five internal strands, finite axioms cut the strand split to {(3,2), (4,1)}, and the (3,2) branch reproduces one Standard Model generation with its hypercharges.
explanation: Think of a particle's internal state as a row of switches, each recording whether one internal strand - an internal null direction - is occupied. The states form an exterior algebra: each strand is filled at most once, like fermions. The principle proposes exactly five strands, split into p protected color-like strands and q strands that mass-generating turns may use. Four finite requirements - chirality protection, anomaly cancellation, an allowed mass channel, and integer index protection - force five strands and leave only two splits, (3,2) and (4,1). One extra infrared input (roughly, that electromagnetism exists) selects (3,2), whose occupancy bookkeeping matches one Standard Model generation, including hypercharges -1/3 and 1/2 and the Z_6 charge lattice. This is a pre-registered conjecture with stated kill conditions, not an established derivation.
why: If it holds, the Standard Model's particle content would become a consequence of counting internal null directions rather than an input - the project's sharpest structural claim about matter. It also connects to known exterior-algebra descriptions of a generation (the Lambda C^5 of grand unification, Furey's ladder construction), giving it independent anchors.
example: In the (3,2) split, occupying strands on the 3-side builds color states while the 2-side carries weak turns; the fully empty and fully filled states are the neutral singlets, and the per-strand hypercharges come out as -1/3 (color side) and 1/2 (weak side).
conventions: The degeneracy label (p, q) means the five strands split into p protected strands (confined factor, complex representations) and q turn-accessible strands. Claim label: pre-registered conjecture conditional on the named finite axioms (A)-(D) plus the tiebreaker (F); the mathematics alone delivers the two-point degeneracy space {(3,2), (4,1)}, not a unique answer. Three generations, mass values, and anything spectral are explicitly NOT fixed by this principle.

summary: In this project, a null tick is one discrete lightlike step of duration epsilon in a 1+1 walk; the kernel-checked identity tau^2 = 4 epsilon^2 nPlus nMinus gives the proper time of a history with nPlus right and nMinus left ticks, timelike exactly when both are nonzero.
explanation: Picture a walker that moves only at light speed, in ticks of duration epsilon, each tick going either right or left along the light cone. After nPlus right ticks and nMinus left ticks, the endpoint displacement gives an elapsed proper time obeying tau^2 = 4 epsilon^2 nPlus nMinus. If all ticks go one way, tau = 0: the path is lightlike and no internal clock advances. As soon as both directions appear, tau > 0: zigzagging between the two null directions is what opens up time. Balanced counts nPlus = nMinus uniquely maximize tau for a given number of ticks. The identity is endpoint geometry only: it does not assign positive proper time to individual null segments, and it is not a claim that counting reversals defines time.
why: It is the simplest quantitative expression of the program's core intuition that massive, aging matter behaves like trapped light. In the repo it is a kernel-checked finite identity that also recovers the textbook time-dilation formula tau^2 = t^2 (1 - v^2) for nonempty histories.
example: With epsilon = 1, a history of 3 right ticks and 3 left ticks has tau^2 = 4 * 3 * 3 = 36, so tau = 6, equal to the coordinate duration t = 6 (the walker is at rest on average); 6 right ticks alone give tau = 0.
conventions: Stated in 1+1 dimensions with units c = 1; tick duration epsilon > 0; nPlus and nMinus count ticks along the two future null directions; coordinate time t = epsilon (nPlus + nMinus) and displacement x = epsilon (nPlus - nMinus). Read strictly as endpoint Lorentzian geometry: one-direction support is null, two-direction support is timelike, and balanced populations uniquely saturate the coordinate-time bound for nonzero tick scale.

summary: NullStrand is this repository's name for the null-edge research program: formalizing in Lean how mass, Dirac operators, gauge structure, and spacetime geometry could emerge from purely lightlike (null) primitives, under strict claim-discipline guardrails.
explanation: NullStrand is a program name - a project codename, not a mathematical object. The program asks how much of known physics can be rebuilt from networks whose elementary steps are all lightlike: mass appears as area opened between null directions, the Dirac operator is assembled on a null-solder frame, and internal charges are conjectured to come from occupied internal null strands. Because the program is speculative, its identity is largely a set of guardrails: results are graded (finite identity, reconstruction, structural theorem, prediction), the Lean kernel is the source of truth, and known dead ends - like diagonal null soldering - are recorded as conventions so agents do not rediscover them. The living orientation note is docs/NULLSTRAND.md; AGENTS.md carries the always-on quick rules.
why: Every draft file, task note, and manuscript in the null-edge tree inherits its conventions from this program, so knowing what NullStrand does and does not claim is the first step to reading the repo honestly. The near-term target is a dual-soldered finite null-edge Dirac algebra presented as a formalization result, not a completed physical theory.
example: A guardrail in action: the operator architecture is fixed as sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_ell_a (differentiate along null edges, solder with dual covectors), and reviving the retired diagonal form sum_a c(ell_a^flat) nabla_ell_a is a convention violation because its symbol is traceless.
conventions: Program-wide conventions are the content: dual soldering, not diagonal soldering; keep spacetime chirality, internal grading, and form degree separate; retardedness alone is not a no-doubling proof; Krein self-adjointness does not by itself prove positivity or stability; emergence claims must say which half of the Malament split (conformal class versus scale) they address; physics claims carry explicit labels such as finite identity, reconstruction, or prediction.

summary: In this project, an obstruction map B sends configurations of a structure to a failure space so that ker B is exactly the massless or symmetric locus and B^dagger B gives the quadratic mass; every mass claim must name its B and show B is canonical, not fitted after the fact.
explanation: The project explains many kinds of mass with one template. Choose a map B that measures how far a configuration fails to stay in a special free condition: a null bundle failing to stay on one direction, a fermion field pairing its left and right components, a gauge push failing to preserve the Higgs vacuum. Configurations that B sends to zero are exactly the massless, gapless, or unbroken ones; away from that zero set, the squared size |B x|^2 - formally the operator B^dagger B - is the quadratic mass or stiffness. The crucial requirement is that B be canonical: forced by the geometry, representation theory, or gauge covariance of the structure, never reverse-engineered from a known mass. A map chosen after the answer is known is just relabeling.
why: This is the program's locked umbrella language for mass, letting a finite Pluecker identity, the Yukawa mechanism, W/Z orbit stiffness, and the Higgs potential curvature be compared sector by sector without pretending they are one theorem. It also disciplines claims: each sector's status (finite identity, reconstruction, structural theorem) is tracked per map.
example: The electroweak instance is B_EW(X) = X H_0 on gauge generators X, with H_0 the Higgs vacuum: ker B_EW is the unbroken electromagnetic direction and |X H_0|^2 gives the W/Z stiffness. The Pluecker instance is B_Pl(Psi) = (psi_i wedge psi_j), zero exactly on collinear (massless) null bundles.
conventions: Locked wording: say 'mass as quadratic obstruction by a canonical obstruction map B'; reserve 'spectral gap' for genuine operator spectra, Hessians, Hamiltonians, or Dirac squares. Every mass claim names its pair (S, B) - the structure and its map - plus a claim label. No double counting: the null/kinetic Pluecker term and the internal Higgs/Yukawa term must match as K_null = Phi_H^2, not add as two independent masses for the same fermion.
notation: B : Conf(S) -> Fail(S); ker B; B^dagger B

summary: In this project's electroweak reconstruction, orbit stiffness is the quadratic cost q(X) = |X H_0|^2 of moving the Higgs vacuum H_0 along a gauge direction X; its rank (target 3) counts the massive W/Z directions and its kernel is the photon's unbroken stabilizer line.
explanation: Picture the Higgs vacuum as a marble resting in a circular valley of possible field values. Gauge transformations push the marble; some directions slide it along the valley floor at no cost, others try to lift it up the wall. Orbit stiffness measures the quadratic cost of each infinitesimal gauge push X through the map X -> X H_0: if X H_0 = 0 the push does nothing - a stabilizer direction that stays massless, the photon - while directions with X H_0 != 0 acquire stiffness |X H_0|^2, and these become the W and Z bosons. The reconstruction's structural claim is a rank and stabilizer count: with the Standard Model electroweak group and Higgs representation assumed, exactly three directions are stiff and a one-dimensional electromagnetic stabilizer survives.
why: It recasts gauge-boson mass generation in the project's canonical-obstruction template without the misleading phrase 'the symmetry breaks': the Higgs defines a covariant internal reference section, and pushes failing to preserve it pay quadratic cost. In the repo this has structural-theorem status, conditional on the assumed group, representation, and vacuum section - a reconstruction, not a prediction.
example: With H_0 = (0, v/sqrt(2)) and X ranging over the four electroweak generators, the three combinations that become W+, W-, and Z give X H_0 != 0, while the electric-charge combination Q = T_3 + Y/2 annihilates H_0 and stays massless.
conventions: Higgs hypercharge Y(H) = 1, electric charge Q = T_3 + Y/2, vacuum H_0 = (0, v/sqrt(2)), obstruction B_EW(X) = X H_0, target ker B_EW = u(1)_em with rank q = 3 where q(X) = |X H_0|^2. Locked separation: W/Z masses live in orbit stiffness or link stiffness, never in the fermion Yukawa block. Prefer gauge-invariant (FMS-style) composite language for physical W/Z excitations.

summary: In this project's Gate C1 analysis, origin polarization asks whether a gauge-safe involution T0 can split the chirality-balanced kernel of the lattice Dirac symbol at zero momentum down to a single Weyl line; existence versus no-go is the decisive fork for a chiral release.
explanation: The project's bare null-edge lattice operator has a problem at zero momentum: its kernel there contains equal left-handed and right-handed pieces, perfectly balanced. To describe Standard-Model-like matter, one handedness must be isolated - the kernel must be polarized to a single Weyl line. Origin polarization is the question of whether an operator T0 native to the model can do this: T0 must square to one, be Hermitian, commute with every gauge transformation, and still have a nonzero chiral trace on the origin kernel. A proved obstacle sharpens the fork: the balanced kernel carries a symmetry J that flips chirality, and any projector commuting with J has zero chiral index, so a working T0 must escape J's commutant. If no native T0 exists, the program must pivot to projected-overlap or domain-wall constructions.
why: This is the mandatory open gate (C1) standing between the program and any Standard-Model-facing claim: species health (Gate C0) is plausibly settled by scalar Wilson-type gaps, but only origin polarization can deliver a single chirality. Framing it as a finite decision problem - escape hatch versus no-go - turns it into a sharp theorem target instead of open-ended churn.
example: The escape-hatch requirements read: T0^2 = 1, T0^dagger = T0, [T0, gauge] = 0, and Tr(Gamma0 (1 + T0)/2) != 0 on K0 = ker D_+(0), where Gamma0 is the origin chirality. A scalar Wilson term fails automatically: being scalar on the origin corner, it commutes with the balance symmetry and cannot shift the chiral count (the C88 taste no-go).
conventions: Gauge-safe means commuting with the gauge action. Balanced means the balance symmetry J obeys J Gamma0 J^-1 = -Gamma0 on the origin kernel, forcing zero chiral index for anything in J's commutant. Any eventual release must respect the ghost rule: no gauge-charged branch may be removed solely by a propagator zero; removal needs a true inverse-propagator mass gap. This is an open program question, not a result.

summary: In this project's dynamics layer, the pair kick is a supplied reversible interaction gate on a four-mode fermionic cell: an even quartic operator that reads the complex Pluecker phase z on the two-particle sector, a second phase reader beyond the free walk.
explanation: The free null walk already senses the modulus of the complex area datum z and, via transport, its relative phase. The pair kick is a second, deliberately supplied ingredient: an interaction acting on a small cell of four fermionic modes at once. It is quartic - built from four creation and annihilation operators - and even, meaning it preserves particle-number parity, so single particles pass through untouched while a pair occupying the cell picks up an update controlled by the phase of z. Kernel-checked results show the kick is exactly reversible, preserves the finite many-particle inner product, fixes every one-particle basis state, and acts nontrivially on an explicit two-particle state. Up to a global phase it is the quarter-period pulse of a Hermitian generator K(z) obeying the same cubic closure, K(z)^3 = |z|^2 K(z), as the derived rest operator.
why: It shows the Pluecker phase is physically readable at the interaction level, not only in free two-site spectra - a single real mass parameter cannot reproduce its interference pattern. The honesty boundary matters equally: the kick is supplied, not derived from a microscopic principle, and whether the free walk forces this interaction is a named open problem.
example: In the supplied pair-kick sector the model produces an exact 4/5-versus-1 interference split that a scalar mass coin cannot mimic, because one real number carries no orientation phase to interfere with.
conventions: Even means particle-number-parity preserving; quartic means degree four in the fermionic ladder operators; support is one four-mode cell consistent with the canonical anticommutation relations and the layer schedule. Status convention: the gate's exactness properties (unitarity, reversibility, sector preservation) are kernel-checked, but the gate itself is an input of the dynamics layer, and no lemma relates its generator K(z) to the one-particle rest operator B_w.

summary: In this project's two-site model, the phase defect is Delta = z_R - (wbar)^2 z_L: the gauge-invariant mismatch between a local complex mass datum z_R and the neighbor's z_L parallel-transported through the edge phase w; its modulus splits the exact free two-site spectrum.
explanation: Each site of the model carries a complex mass datum z - an area with an orientation phase - and the link between two sites carries a transport phase w. Neither phase is observable by itself: changing the local frame at a site rotates its z, and a phase common to both sites can be removed outright. What survives every such change of bookkeeping is the mismatch Delta = z_R - (wbar)^2 z_L, which compares the right site's datum with the left one after carrying it across the edge. The squared energy levels of the exact two-site Hamiltonian are |z_L|^2 + t^2 +/- t |Delta| for hopping strength t, so a nonzero defect visibly splits the spectrum, and the lower level touches zero exactly at t = |z_L| with z_R = -(wbar)^2 z_L.
why: It proves that the orientation phase of the null-spinor area is physical rather than gauge bookkeeping: a transported relative phase is a free one-particle observable, the key step separating the derived complex mass from a single real mass parameter. Once the phase varies around a closed cycle, the same data become patched link data with an integer winding.
example: Take w = 1, t = 1, z_L = 1, and z_R = e^(i*phi): the defect modulus is 2 |sin(phi/2)|, so at phi = 0 the two squared levels coincide, while at phi = pi (z_R = -z_L) the lower squared energy reaches exactly zero.
conventions: Definition: Delta = z_R - (wbar)^2 z_L, with wbar the complex conjugate of the unit edge phase w. The square on wbar is forced by weight: under a local chiral frame change b at a site, that site's datum transforms as z -> b^2 z, and |Delta| is invariant under independent local chiral-frame changes. The exact spectrum theorem assumes t >= 0, |w| = 1, and equal moduli |z_L| = |z_R|; the equal-modulus hypothesis is load-bearing - the formal development contains an explicit unequal-modulus counterexample.

summary: In this project, Plucker disagreement is det P, the determinant of the summed rank-one null momenta of a bundle; it measures how far the null directions are from all pointing the same way, and it equals the bundle's invariant mass squared.
explanation: Take several massless signals, each described by a two-component null spinor psi. Each contributes a rank-one 2x2 Hermitian momentum block psi psi^dagger, and the bundle's total momentum is the sum P of these blocks. The determinant det P is the Plucker disagreement. If every signal points in exactly the same lightlike direction, the sum is still rank one and det P = 0: the bundle is massless. The moment the directions differ, det P becomes strictly positive. Picture flashlight beams: perfectly parallel beams behave like one massless beam, while beams splayed apart carry an invariant spread that no observer can remove by changing frames. In this draft research program that spread is read as mass squared, and for two edges it also equals linear entropy and concurrence squared.
why: It packages mass as a single frame-invariant number measuring relational geometry rather than a substance. In this repo it is the organizing quantity of the null-edge program: the kernel-checked Plucker mass theorem identifies det P with the total pairwise wedge spread of the null directions.
example: Two null spinors psi = (1,0) and phi = (0,1) give P = diag(1,0) + diag(0,1) = I, so det P = 1: maximal disagreement, invariant mass 1. If instead phi = (2,0), the directions agree, P = diag(5,0), and det P = 0: still massless.
conventions: The invariant statement lives at the unnormalized level: det P = m^2 with P the raw momentum sum. Normalized density matrices only know the ratio m/E; the project locks the language 'Plucker norm / unnormalized concurrence' and forbids claiming frame invariance for det rho. The trusted core proves m^2 is real and nonnegative.
notation: det P, det P_tot, det(sum_i psi_i psi_i^dagger)
source_refs: Grassmann-Pluecker coordinates, classical projective line geometry

summary: The project's trusted core theorem: det(sum_i psi_i psi_i^dagger) equals the sum over pairs of |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2, so the invariant mass squared of a finite bundle of null spinors is exactly its total pairwise null-direction disagreement; kernel-checked in Lean.
explanation: Plucker mass is the project's name for mass obtained purely from lightlike ingredients. A massless degree of freedom is a two-component null spinor psi, contributing momentum psi psi^dagger. For any finite bundle of these, the theorem says the determinant of the summed momentum, which is the invariant mass squared, equals the sum over all pairs of the squared wedge product |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2, a number measuring how much each pair of light directions differs. Think of mass as the total misalignment score of a swarm of light rays: one ray, or many perfectly aligned rays, score zero; any splay scores positive. The identity, together with the exact massless criterion (zero if and only if all directions are projectively collinear), is kernel-checked in trusted Lean code with no proof gaps.
why: It is the strongest trusted result of the null-edge program and the core the mechanism paper P1 is built on: invariant mass emerges as relational geometry of null data rather than an inserted parameter. The project explicitly does not claim that all physical mass is literally one Plucker spread; that wider reading stays a draft program interpretation.
example: For two spinors the identity reads det(psi psi^dagger + phi phi^dagger) = |psi wedge phi|^2; with psi = (1,0) and phi = (0,1) both sides equal 1, and both vanish exactly when phi is a scalar multiple of psi.
conventions: det P = m^2 holds at the unnormalized momentum level; only m/E survives normalization. The wedge of two spinors is the 2x2 determinant psi_1 phi_2 - psi_2 phi_1 of their components. Trusted statements include: a single null edge is massless, m^2 is real and nonnegative, and m^2 = 0 iff all directions coincide; the twistor-chart matching carries its own pinned normalization.
notation: det(sum_i psi_i psi_i^dagger) = sum_{i<j} |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2

summary: The Gate I1 core result of the project's NERD roadmap: a two-edge Pluecker/Cauchy-Binet identity expressing mass squared as the determinant of summed null-edge momentum data, det P = m^2, ported to kernel-checked Lean draft code with a fixed build order.
explanation: In the NERD roadmap, the Pluecker mass identity is the entry gate (I1) of the whole program: before anything about walks, gauge fields, or gravity, the repo pins down in Lean that the determinant of a sum of two rank-one null momentum blocks equals the squared wedge (the Pluecker coordinate) of the two spinors, which is the invariant mass squared. The proof route is deliberately staged: soldering determinant first, then the positive-semidefinite future cone, then rank and null structure, then the 2xn Cauchy-Binet step that turns the determinant of a product into a sum of squared 2x2 minors, then a kinematic cross-check. It is the same mathematics as the general Plucker mass theorem, packaged as a buildable gate with a recorded axiom footprint.
why: Cauchy-Binet is the classical linear-algebra engine behind every mass-equals-area claim in the program, so landing this gate first protects everything downstream. It also anchors the normalized dictionary (det rho = m^2/4E^2, concurrence = m/E) and the first-order bridge (gamma dot P)^2 = det(P) times identity.
example: Write P = A A^dagger where A is the 2xn matrix whose columns are the spinors psi_i; Cauchy-Binet gives det P = sum over column pairs of |det of the 2x2 submatrix (psi_i psi_j)|^2, which is exactly the sum of squared wedges.
conventions: The invariant statement holds only at the unnormalized level: det P = m^2. Normalized single-edge states know only m/E; the roadmap locks the phrase 'Plucker norm / unnormalized concurrence' and forbids claiming frame invariance for det rho. The Gate I1 port is kernel-checked draft code with axiom footprint propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
source_refs: Cauchy-Binet determinant formula, classical linear algebra

summary: In the project's area-to-Dirac-gap manuscript, the Plucker mass operator B_z is the 2x2 odd Hermitian matrix [[0, z], [conj(z), 0]] built from the complex wedge z of two null spinors; it squares to det(P_tot) times the identity and supplies the walk's mass term.
explanation: Two null spinors psi and phi determine one complex number z = psi wedge phi, their Pluecker coordinate. The draft manuscript promotes this number to a matrix: B_z has zeros on the diagonal and z, conj(z) off the diagonal. Because its entries sit off-diagonal, B_z swaps the two chirality components into each other - it is odd for the grading Gamma = diag(1,-1) and anticommutes with Gamma - exactly the way a mass term in the Dirac equation couples left- and right-handed parts. Its square is |z|^2 times the identity, and |z|^2 = det P_tot, so the operator remembers precisely the invariant mass and nothing else. A classification theorem in the draft shows the odd Hermitian square roots of mu^2 times identity form a single phase circle, so B_z is canonical up to phase.
why: It is the bridge object of the program's flagship draft: it turns the static mass-equals-area identity into dynamics, since H_z(k) = k Gamma + B_z has relativistic dispersion and exponentiating B_z gives an exactly unitary null-step walk. The point is that the mass term is not inserted by hand - it is built from null geometry.
example: For z = i, B_z = [[0, i], [-i, 0]], which is minus the Pauli matrix sigma_y; then B_z^2 = I and H_z(k) = k sigma_z + B_z has eigenvalues +/- sqrt(k^2 + 1).
conventions: Grading Gamma = diag(1,-1); explicitly B_z = Re(z) sigma_x - Im(z) sigma_y, Hermitian and Gamma-odd. Phase covariance: rotating the phase of z conjugates B_z by a unitary (W_u B_z W_u^dagger = B_{uz}), so only |z| is spectrally meaningful, and both SL(2,C) spinor rescaling conventions induce the same conjugation. Draft-manuscript object, not established physics.
notation: B_z = [[0, z], [conj(z), 0]]; B_z^2 = |z|^2 I = det(P_tot) I

summary: In the project's convention ledger, the Plucker obstruction is the canonical map B_Pl(Psi) = (psi_i wedge psi_j) for i < j, sending a bundle of null spinors to all its pairwise wedges; its squared norm is the invariant mass squared and its kernel the massless locus.
explanation: The project organizes every mass claim as 'mass as quadratic obstruction by a canonical obstruction map B': a natural map B from configurations to a failure space, where the kernel of B is the massless or symmetric locus and B^dagger B gives the quadratic cost of leaving it. The Plucker obstruction is the flagship instance. Feed in a list Psi of null spinors; out comes the vector of all pairwise wedge products. If the list is projectively collinear - every ray along one light direction - all wedges vanish and B_Pl(Psi) = 0. Otherwise the squared length of B_Pl(Psi) is exactly det P, the invariant mass squared. So mass is literally the obstruction to sharing a single null direction, with no fitted parameters anywhere in the map.
why: It gives paper P1 its locked umbrella language and slots the Plucker mechanism into a uniform ledger beside B_Y (Yukawa reconstruction), B_EW (electroweak structural theorem), and B_Higgs (potential Hessian), each with its own claim grade. Mathematically it is a rank-one obstruction: the wedges vanish exactly on the rank-one locus.
example: Psi = (psi_1, psi_2, psi_3) gives B_Pl(Psi) = (psi_1 wedge psi_2, psi_1 wedge psi_3, psi_2 wedge psi_3), and the sum of the three squared moduli equals det(sum_i psi_i psi_i^dagger).
conventions: Locked language: for P1 use 'finite invariant mass', 'rank-one obstruction', or 'quadratic Plucker obstruction' - never 'spectral gap', which is reserved for operator spectra. No double counting: the Plucker/null-spread term is the kinetic null-bundle side and the Higgs/Yukawa term the internal zero-order side; operator matching is K_null = Phi_H^2, never m_Plucker^2 + m_Higgs^2 added as two explanations of one fermion mass.

summary: In this project, the positive sector is a chosen subspace of the constraint cohomology that is invariant under the mass operator D and positive for the Krein form J; physical states are declared to live there, and the choice is extra decoder data, not canonically supplied.
explanation: The program's state spaces start out with an indefinite inner product (a Krein space): some vectors have positive length squared, some negative, some zero. After quotienting away redundant gauge descriptions using the nilpotent charge Q - forming the cohomology H_Q = ker Q / range Q - the leftover form is still indefinite, and an indefinite space has no preferred positive half, just as a saddle surface has no built-in choice of uphill directions. A positive sector is a deliberately chosen nonzero subspace P of H_Q that the mass operator D preserves and on which the Krein form J is positive. Particles are then modeled as stable eigen-modes inside this chosen sector. The project stresses that this is additional decoder data: existence is model-dependent and uniqueness is not expected.
why: It separates what the mathematics supplies for free (cohomology with a well-defined indefinite form) from what a physical interpretation must add (a positive home for states), blocking a common over-claim. Explicit repo witnesses show the same cohomology class flips to negative under one Krein sign change, so positivity really is independent input.
example: In the repo's PositiveHodgeDecoder witness, a non-exact harmonic class e2 is positive and satisfies D#D e2 = mu^2 e2, giving a spectral mass; reversing one Krein sign makes the very same class negative.
conventions: Positivity is relative to the chosen Krein sign matrix J and rides on the load-bearing hypothesis Q# = Q (Krein self-adjoint charge). Requiring the sector to be maximal is natural but not forced. Keep three operators distinct: Q removes redundancy, Q^*Q + QQ^* (Hilbert adjoint) picks harmonic representatives, and D#D (Krein adjoint) supplies spectral mass; collapsing them would make every physical class a zero mode.

summary: In this project's causal-order work, a probe tetrad is a basis of a rank-four natural probe subspace over a finite causal order; once one frame's pairing matrix is diag(1,-1,-1,-1), the allowed normalized frame changes are exactly the eta-orthogonal (Lorentz) maps.
explanation: The nullstrand program tries to read geometry out of a bare web of causal relations. Individual probe functions cannot be natural: on a highly symmetric order, every probe respected by all symmetries is constant. What can be natural is a probe subspace - a small space of functions transported by order symmetries up to change of basis. When such a subspace has rank four, any basis of it is called a probe tetrad, a finite stand-in for the four reference directions (one time, three space) of a spacetime frame. Pairing the probes gives a symmetric matrix G, and switching frames transforms it by congruence, G to M^T G M. If one frame produces the Minkowski matrix diag(1,-1,-1,-1), the frame changes preserving it are precisely the Lorentz transformations, so Lorentz gauge freedom appears as basis freedom.
why: It identifies the correct finite Lorentz-gauge quotient for causal-order probes, a needed step toward deriving spacetime structure instead of assuming it. The repo flags the limits: the current rank four comes from event cardinality (a five-event antichain), not causal dimension, and nothing yet proves physical carriers have Lorentzian inertia.
example: The canonical zero-sum subspace on a five-event antichain has rank four; a probe tetrad is any basis of it, and its corrected pairing matrices in two frames obey G_c = M^T G_b M.
conventions: Project metric matrix diag(1,-1,-1,-1), signature (+,-,-,-); eta-orthogonal means M^T eta M = eta. Guardrail from AGENTS.md: universal null frames must come from decorated tetrad/spin-frame data unless a separate theorem derives them - never claim a bare graph canonically supplies a tetrad. Variance matters: scaling operator lengths by r scales the corrected-pairing Gram matrix by r^-2 (it behaves as an inverse metric), while the row-coframe metric scales by r^2.
notation: G_c = M^T G_b M; eta = diag(1,-1,-1,-1)

summary: In this project, refinement is subdividing a finite complex or carrier into a finer one on the way toward the continuum; a finite structure or channel interpretation counts as physics only if it survives refinement, and refinement functoriality is a candidate rigidity constraint.
explanation: The null-edge program builds everything from deliberately small finite objects: complexes with a handful of edges, carriers with a few channels. Refinement is the operation of replacing such an object by a finer version of itself - subdividing edges, adding events, shrinking the mesh - the way a coarse pixel grid is replaced by a finer one when approximating a smooth image. It is the road toward a continuum limit, taken one step at a time. The program's discipline is that finite results are only candidate physics: a named structure, such as the aperture, closure, turn, and soldering channels of the carrier square, earns physical meaning only if it persists coherently as the complex is refined, ideally functorially - refine then compute should agree with compute then refine.
why: It is the main honesty gate between finite mathematics and physical claims: per the future-directions document, the channel names become physics only if finite carriers refine to continuum gauge/Dirac systems. Refinement functoriality is also one of the candidate constraints that could make the four-channel carrier decomposition rigid.
example: The soldering covariance module SolderingLocalFrameCovariance passes an exact refinement law, while the vacuum-shift redundancy results are explicitly flagged as open under refinement and the continuum limit.
conventions: Direction of the arrow: refinement subdivides toward finer complexes, the opposite of coarse-graining or decimation. Results proved at one fixed finite size keep an in-paper or finite claim label until a refinement law for them is actually proven.

summary: In the project's finite Dirac-walk draft, the rest gap is the walk's energy at zero momentum, equal to the modulus |z| of the complex Pluecker area of two null spinors; it plays the role of rest mass, and the full spectral band gap at rest is 2|z|.
explanation: A free particle's energy depends on its momentum k. For the finite walk generated by H_z(k) = k Gamma + B_z, the two energy branches are plus and minus sqrt(k^2 + |z|^2) - the same hyperbola shape as the relativistic energy-momentum relation. At k = 0 the branches sit at +|z| and -|z|: they do not touch unless z = 0. That opening at zero momentum is the rest gap. It behaves exactly like rest mass: it is the minimum energy cost of the excitation, it bends the dispersion from a straight light-cone V into a hyperbola, and it vanishes precisely when the two null spinors are collinear, which is when the Pluecker area z is zero.
why: It closes the program's loop from statics to dynamics: the same number whose square is det P_tot in the Plucker mass identity reappears as an honest spectral gap of an exactly unitary walk, supporting the reading that mass-as-null-disagreement is dynamical and not just bookkeeping. Draft-manuscript status, not established physics.
example: With |z| = 1 the spectrum of H_z(k) is +/- sqrt(k^2 + 1): rest energy 1, band gap 2 at k = 0, and group velocity below 1 everywhere - a massive relativistic dispersion built from purely null ingredients.
conventions: Terminology care: the rest gap (rest energy) is |z|, while the full band gap between the two branches at rest is 2|z| - the manuscript uses both figures, so state which is meant. mu = |z| = sqrt(det P_tot); grading Gamma = diag(1,-1). Only |z| is invariant: changing the phase of z conjugates B_z by a unitary and leaves the spectrum unchanged.
notation: rest gap = |z|; spectrum of H_z(k) = +/- sqrt(k^2 + |z|^2)

summary: In this project's zigzag model, retardedness is the rule that every light-speed step moves forward in time only; a program identity shows this forward-only bias acts exactly like a hidden Wilson term in the model's dispersion relation.
explanation: Picture the 1+1 dimensional zigzag walker: at every tick it hops one step left or right at light speed, and it never moves backward in time. That forward-only rule is called retardedness. It looks like an innocent causality assumption, but in this project it does real mathematical work. Lattice field theorists normally add an extra term by hand, the Wilson term, to remove unwanted duplicate particles called doublers. An exact dispersion identity in the program says the zigzag model's retardedness IS such a Wilson term in disguise: the forward-in-time bias supplies the doubler-suppressing correction automatically, and the zigzag transfer operator satisfies an exact Ginsparg-Wilson relation, so chirality is tracked honestly through the discretization.
why: It ties a causality-flavored modeling choice to the standard machinery of lattice field theory, which is how physicists argue a discrete model has a healthy continuum story. In this project it tightens the claim that the 1+1D 'mass is the amplitude to turn' result survives discretization with exact chiral bookkeeping.
example: In the exactly solved 1+1D case, the zigzag transfer operator obeys a Ginsparg-Wilson relation with R = 1/2 whose grading is chirality composed with spatial reflection (edge-orientation reversal); the dispersion contains the same momentum-dependent correction a Wilson fermion would have, but nobody put it in by hand.
conventions: Project guardrail (AGENTS.md): retardedness alone is not a no-doubling proof; it rules out coefficient-zero doublers, but determinant-level tests must inspect det D(q) = 0 or the corresponding mass-shell condition. The Wilson-term identity is a draft-grade program result, not established physics.

summary: Scale selection is the open problem of deriving an absolute mass scale rather than mass ratios; a kernel-checked no-go in this project proves that no positive, fixed, finite action scaling homogeneously with positive degree can make a nonzero configuration stationary.
explanation: A theory can often predict ratios, like one mass being twice another, without ever saying how heavy anything is in actual units. Fixing the actual number is scale selection. The project's no-go works like this: suppose the action S (the quantity histories try to make stationary) is positive and homogeneous, meaning S(t x) = t^p S(x) when you rescale everything by t, with degree p > 0. Then the derivative in the scaling direction at t = 1 is p S(x) > 0, never zero, so no nonzero configuration can be stationary: the system always prefers to shrink. The project's quartic Pluecker action, with S(t psi, t phi; x) = t^4 S(psi, phi; x), is the live instance. Selecting a scale therefore requires an extra dimensionful input.
why: It explains, as a theorem rather than an excuse, why this program predicts counts, signs, ratios, and phases but stays silent on absolute masses. It also disciplines future claims: any proposal to derive an absolute scale must display a running family, competing homogeneity, constraint, ensemble scale, or other dimensionful input that evades the no-go.
example: The control potential V_c(t) = (t^2 - c)^2 has stationary points exactly at t = 0 and t^2 = c; with the supplied input c = 1, the nonzero minima t = 1 and t = -1 exist - so selection is possible, but its magnitude is exactly the new input c, not a prediction.
conventions: The no-go assumes the action is positive, finite, fixed (not running), and homogeneous of natural degree p > 0; at p = 0 the radial direction is exactly flat, which also cannot select an isolated scale. Kernel-checked at the stated generality, inside a draft research program.

summary: In this project, a Selector is any extra structure - a metric, a trace, an invariant - proposed to pick out one preferred channel decomposition of the carrier operator's square from the many equivalent ones; kernel-checked theorems show most natural candidates fail.
explanation: The carrier operator's square splits into named channels (aperture, closure, turn, soldering), but the finite algebra alone does not force that naming: many different splits present the same operator. A Selector is a proposed tie-breaker, some intrinsic structure that would single out the physical decomposition. The project has tested candidates and killed several with exact counterexamples: raw solder degree fails because an idempotent operator makes a degree-two word and its degree-four square evaluate identically; every scalar linear functional that ignores commutators is just a multiple of trace, and an explicit trace-zero direction makes it noninjective; componentwise matrix trace is preserved by a nonzero shear. Positive variational selection works, but only after a channel metric is supplied by hand, which relocates the question instead of answering it.
why: Whether a Selector exists decides if the program's channel names (its candidate 'forces') are canonical facts or coordinate choices. Either outcome is publishable: a surviving intrinsic Selector would rigidify the decomposition, while a sharp residual-ambiguity no-go would turn carrier non-rigidity into an honest gauge freedom.
example: The weighted-barycentric theorem: for scalar channels, every positive diagonal quadratic cost has a unique minimizer, but equal weights choose (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) while weights (1, 2, 3) choose (6/11, 3/11, 2/11) for the same unit total - convex minimization selects a decomposition only after a channel metric is chosen.
conventions: Project coinage from the Paper F lane; surviving candidate routes are nonlinear spectral data, vector-valued invariants, locality, a derived positive physical sector, and information monotones. A separate 'Spin(10) selector' lane uses the same word for a different uniqueness problem about pure-spinor stabilizers.

summary: Soldering attaches a Clifford algebra direction label (a covector alpha^a) to each finite-difference direction of a lattice Dirac operator; in this project the locked architecture is dual soldering, D_N = sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_{ell_a}, never the diagonal form.
explanation: A discrete derivative on a graph knows which direction it differences along, but a Dirac operator also needs to know which Clifford algebra element multiplies that difference. Soldering is the rule that attaches an algebraic direction label, a Clifford covector alpha^a, to each concrete difference direction. Think of legs and shoes: each leg of the operator steps along a graph direction ell_a, and soldering fits it with an algebraic shoe c(alpha^a) so the spinor algebra knows what that step means. In continuum geometry the tetrad plays this role. In this project the locked choice is dual soldering: the steps are null directions ell_a, but the Clifford labels are the dual covectors alpha^a of the null-solder frame, giving D_N = sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_{ell_a}.
why: Soldering is what turns a bare graph difference operator into a genuine Dirac operator with the correct continuum symbol. The project's dual-versus-diagonal soldering result (the trace obstruction) is one of its sharpest locked conventions and shapes every downstream operator statement.
example: In the active operator D_N = sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_{ell_a}, the finite differences nabla_{ell_a} step along the null directions ell_a of a simplex frame while the Clifford actions c(alpha^a) use the dual covectors alpha^a; the diagonal alternative c(ell_a^flat) fails the trace/symbol audit.
conventions: Locked: the active Dirac architecture is dual-soldered, D_N = sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_{ell_a}. The diagonal form sum_a c(ell_a^flat) nabla_{ell_a} must not be revived as the continuum Dirac symbol; its trace obstruction is a program convention. Under the Malament split, the soldering Gram data owes exactly the scale/volume half of geometry, no more and no less.

summary: In this project, the spiral layer is the kernel-checked answer to 'does mass zigzag or spiral': the magnitude of mass is blind to orientation (the zigzag reading), while phase, spin transport, and CP/matter-antimatter content live entirely in oriented data (the spiral reading).
explanation: The program's founding picture had two rival cartoons of a massive particle: a zigzag that bounces back and forth between two light-speed directions, and a spiral that additionally corkscrews with a definite handedness. The spiral layer is a family of about fifteen kernel-checked draft modules that split the question exactly at the finite level. How much mass a history carries turns out to ignore orientation completely - hairpin reversals maximize it per corner - so the zigzag cartoon is right for magnitude. But everything oriented lives in spiral-like data: the quantum phase picked up at corners, how spin is transported, and the CP-odd content that distinguishes matter from antimatter. Corner phases are half solid angles, and the checkerboard corner factor i is now a theorem rather than an input convention.
why: It resolves a foundational ambiguity of the program with theorems instead of taste, and it cleanly locates CP violation: zigzag content is CP-inert at all orders, while CP-odd content equals oriented volume. The same layer produced the exact kink-cost law and the perimeter-versus-area crossover for framed Wilson loops.
example: A smooth loop costs only phase (the hemisphere Berry sign -1/4 is a kernel fact), while a kink costs magnitude: the k-kink penalty is exactly (1/2)^k, and the crossover between kink-dominated and area-dominated cost sits at k* = sigma A / log 2.
conventions: Draft-grade, guard-pinned results on finite complexes; continuum limits, Lorentz recovery, and physical Yukawa/CKM/QCD values are explicitly not claimed. The corner factor i follows the project's quarter-turn lune convention, proved in the SpinCornerFourCycleAristotle module.

summary: In this project, a strand is an internal charge-label slot carried on a carrier edge; the list of occupied strands records which internal charges an excitation carries, and generations are conjectured to share strand occupancy while differing as projective-coherence modules.
explanation: Think of each edge of the finite carrier complex as a cable that can contain several labeled wires. Each wire slot is a strand, and occupying a strand is how an excitation carries an internal charge - the strand list is the particle's charge bookkeeping. Two program pictures lean on this. First, generations: an electron-like and a muon-like state would have the same strand occupancy (identical charges) but sit in the carrier category as inequivalent projective-coherence modules, which is how they can share charges yet differ in mass. Second, dark matter: an excitation with an empty strand list carries no gauge charge and is invisible to forces, yet still participates in soldering and can acquire mass only through seesaw-style leakage.
why: Strands separate 'what charges a particle has' from 'how it sits in the carrier', which is the program's reframing of the generation puzzle: three families as three inequivalent modules over the same charge data, not three copies with bigger masses. The word also echoes in the program name NullStrand.
example: A kernel-checked no-go (FamilyIndexNoGo.count_completions) counts inequivalent positive-sector completions as exactly n + 1 at strand rank n, equal to three exactly when n = 2 - so 'three generations' is not forced by the finite carrier category alone; a rank-fixing input is the missing ingredient.
conventions: The generation and dark-matter readings are conjecture-to-speculative grade (C or spec) in the program's claim calculus; the counting no-go is machine-verified draft. Strand occupancy is program bookkeeping on a finite complex, not an established physical object.

summary: In this project, the graded square of the finite dual-soldered operator D = i D_N + Gamma_s Phi; keeping the spacetime chirality grading, the internal grading, and the form-degree grading distinct is exactly what makes the mass term enter the square as +Phi^2 rather than -Phi^2.
explanation: Squaring a Dirac-type operator D = i D_N + Gamma_s Phi produces a kinetic part from D_N, a mass part from Phi, and cross terms. Whether the mass enters with a plus sign is pure bookkeeping about which pieces commute or anticommute: with Gamma_s squaring to one, anticommuting with the Clifford coefficients C_a, and commuting with the transport nabla_a and with Phi, the cross terms cancel and the square contains +Phi^2. If Phi instead anticommuted with Gamma_s, the sign would flip to -Phi^2. The project therefore locks three separate gradings - spacetime chirality Gamma_s, internal finite grading chi_E, and cochain form degree - and requires the Higgs/Yukawa block to be odd internally but even under Gamma_s, which forces the +Phi^2 convention.
why: The square is the program's draft spine for how mass appears in the finite operator: the kinetic side and the Phi^2 side are matched by an on-shell condition, not added as two independent masses. Conflating the gradings silently corrupts the sign, which is why the separation rule is convention-locked.
example: With the locked hypotheses, D^2 contains the block -Box_null + Phi^2; in mostly-minus signature the mass-shell normalization -Box_null + Phi^2 = 0 gives p^2 = m^2, the standard relativistic energy-momentum relation.
conventions: Locked in docs/CONVENTIONS.md: Phi_H is chi_E-odd internally and commutes with Gamma_s (never Gamma_s-odd), forcing +Phi_H^2. Safe sign hypotheses: Gamma_s^2 = 1, {Gamma_s, C_a} = 0, [Gamma_s, nabla_a] = 0, [Gamma_s, Phi] = 0, [C_a, Phi] = 0. Never use form degree or internal grading to repair a spacetime chirality sign error.

summary: The trace obstruction is a one-line proof that diagonal null soldering fails: any weighted sum of ell_a^flat tensor ell_a over null directions has trace zero, because each ell_a is null, while the identity map it would need to reproduce has trace d, the spacetime dimension.
explanation: A Dirac operator built on null edges needs its Clifford part and its derivative part matched up ('soldered') so that the operator squares to the wave operator. The tempting diagonal recipe uses the same null vector ell_a for both jobs: sum_a c(ell_a^flat) nabla_ell_a. The trace obstruction kills this. The recipe's symbol involves sum_a b_a ell_a^flat tensor ell_a, and the trace of each term is the inner product ell_a . ell_a, which is zero precisely because null vectors have zero length in the spacetime metric. So the whole sum has trace zero no matter how the weights b_a are chosen. But reproducing the identity on covectors, which the correct symbol requires, needs trace d. Zero never equals d, so diagonal soldering can never work.
why: It is the reason the project locked the dual-soldered architecture D_N = sum_a c(alpha^a) nabla_ell_a, in which support comes from null directions ell_a but Clifford soldering comes from dual covectors alpha^a with alpha^a(ell_b) = delta^a_b. A cheap trace computation dictated the program's central operator design.
example: In 1+1 dimensions with mostly-minus metric, ell = (1, 1) is null: ell . ell = 1 - 1 = 0. The matrix ell^flat tensor ell then has trace 0, and adding the other null direction (1, -1) with any weights still gives trace 0 - but the identity on the 2-dimensional cotangent space has trace 2.
conventions: Stated in the project's mostly-minus metric signature; d denotes the spacetime dimension. Locked convention (docs/CONVENTIONS.md): the diagonal architecture appears only as a documented negative comparison, never as the basic Dirac symbol, and the dual-soldered operator is the active architecture.
notation: tr(sum_a b_a ell_a^flat tensor ell_a) = 0 vs tr(id) = d

summary: In this project, a turn is the chirality-flipping channel of the null-edge dynamics: the event where a history reverses its null direction and flips handedness, weighted by the quarter-turn corner amplitude (i eps m) per reversal and gated by a Higgs-shaped resource.
explanation: A massless particle in the model runs along null edges with a fixed handedness (chirality). A turn is the elementary event where the history reverses its null direction and flips that handedness - the corner in the zigzag picture. In the operator language, turns form one of the four channels in the square of the carrier operator (aperture, closure, turn, soldering); the turn block Q_T is the mass channel, entering through the term Gamma phi. In the path-sum language, a history with r reversals picks up exactly the weight (i eps m)^r: one amplitude factor per turn, where eps is the step size and m the mass parameter. The program's WAY-turn no-go argues that flipping chirality while conserving charge requires an extra coherence resource, which is Higgs-shaped.
why: The turn channel is where mass lives in the four-channel decomposition, turning 'why do particles have mass' into 'what permits turns'. The no-go that a closed, charge-conserving system cannot implement the flip alone gives the program its structural reading of the Higgs as the ancilla enabling the chirality gate.
example: In the kernel-checked history algebra (HistoryLocalFourChannelAction), the flat encoding assigns one aperture per step and one turn per reversal, and the quarter-turn weight gives exactly i^r and (i eps m)^r, with a nonzero one-turn witness.
conventions: The corner factor i follows the project quarter-turn lune convention and is now a theorem, not an input; eps is the lattice step and m the mass parameter. The Higgs interpretation is conjecture grade (C) in the program's claim calculus; the finite channel algebra is machine-verified draft (M).

summary: In this project, the turn amplitude is the strength of the chirality flip per step in the carrier/zigzag dynamics; 'mass is the amplitude to turn' is the exactly solved 1+1D statement that this flip amplitude equals the Pluecker wedge measuring null-direction disagreement.
explanation: In the 1+1 dimensional zigzag model, a particle's history is a sequence of light-speed steps that occasionally reverse direction. Each reversal carries a small quantum amplitude; that number is the turn amplitude. A particle that never turns travels at light speed and is massless. A particle that turns often lingers near one place and is heavy. The project's machine-checked bridge identity makes this exact in the solved case: the chirality-flip amplitude equals the wedge, the Pluecker measure of how much the two null directions in the state disagree. The dynamical mass parameter and the kinematic disagreement measure are literally the same number. This is the strongest sense in which the program says mass is not stuff but a rate: the amplitude to turn.
why: It welds the program's kinematic layer (mass as pairwise null-direction disagreement, the trusted Pluecker theorem) to its dynamical layer (mass as rate of chirality exchange) with a single machine-checked equality. It is also the program's headline slogan, so its exact scope - one solved 1+1D case - matters for honesty.
example: The draft lemma onshell_wedge_normSq_eq_coin_sq states the identity: on shell, the squared norm of the wedge equals the square of the coin (flip) parameter; in the pinned dispersion cos w = cos k cos th, the mass coin th is visible as the luminal deficit, and every massive mode is strictly subluminal.
conventions: The per-reversal weight is (i eps m) with the project quarter-turn corner factor i, where eps is the step size and m the mass parameter; the wedge identity is machine-verified in the 1+1D model only - 3+1D packaging is open - and 'mass is the amplitude to turn' must be quoted with that scope.

summary: In this project, which-direction information is the record of which null direction a quantum history took; mass is read as the visible mixedness left in the direction register after that hidden record is traced out - retained distinguishability rather than mere ignorance.
explanation: In the double-slit experiment, anything that records which slit a particle used destroys the interference pattern, even if nobody reads the record. The program applies the same logic to direction. A massless beam is a pure, single-null-direction message: perfectly coherent. When a state contains several disagreeing null directions and the hidden history keeps a record of which one was taken, tracing that record out leaves the direction register in a mixed state. The project's identities make this quantitative: the normalized direction state rho = P / tr P has rank one exactly when the state is massless, and det rho equals the linear entropy, so the amount of mixedness is the mass measure. A coherence matrix Omega interpolates between full interference (Omega = 1) and full mixture (Omega = delta).
why: It recasts the origin of mass as a quantum-information statement - mass as the obstruction to compressing a history ensemble into one pure null-direction message - suggesting entropy-like monotones for mass, and it explains why signed closure can lower mass: it reorganizes coherence rather than adding noise. This framing is conjecture grade, built over machine-verified identities.
example: For two edges with weights w_i and null spinors psi_i: det P = sum over pairs of w_i w_j |psi_i wedge psi_j|^2, and det rho = (1 - tr rho^2) / 2, the linear entropy, which also equals the two-edge concurrence squared - three names for the same retained which-direction record.
conventions: The identities (rho = P / tr P and the determinant-entropy-concurrence equalities) are machine-verified in-paper; the resource-theory reading (free states are coherent null beams, monotones track spectral mass) is a registered conjecture whose kill test is that entropy measures must track spectral mass under the allowed dynamics, not merely rename it.

summary: The repo convention that labels the eight octonion units by 3-bit binary strings e000..e111, multiplies units so the product's label is the bitwise XOR of the input labels, and takes the plus-or-minus sign from a fixed Fano-plane orientation.
explanation: Octonions are 8-dimensional numbers with eight basis units. This project names those units by every 3-bit string, e000 through e111, with e000 the unit 1. Multiplying two units is a two-step recipe: the product's label is the bitwise XOR of the two input labels (compare bit by bit: equal bits give 0, different bits give 1), and a separate sign, read off a fixed orientation of the Fano plane (the seven-point geometry organizing octonion multiplication triples), decides plus or minus. For example, e011 times e111 has label 011 XOR 111 = 100, and the project's orientation makes the answer +e100. The scheme turns index bookkeeping into mechanical bit arithmetic that a computer can validate exhaustively.
why: Octonion multiplication tables differ from author to author, and silently mixing conventions corrupts signs in every downstream formula. Locking one machine-checkable labeling lets all Lean proofs and oracle scripts in this repo agree, and it underlies the octonion layer of the Dixon algebra and the Furey-style particle-state constructions.
example: Anchor products in the repo convention: e011 * e111 = e100, e101 * e111 = e010, e110 * e111 = e001. The label arithmetic is pure XOR: 011 xor 111 = 100, 101 xor 111 = 010, 110 xor 111 = 001.
conventions: This is the project's own convention and is NOT Baez (2002) or Furey (2015) verbatim: any formula from those sources needs explicit basis relabeling AND sign correction via PhysicsSM.Algebra.Octonion.ConventionBridge. The full sign table is validated by Scripts/oracle/validate_octonion.py.
notation: e000, e001, ..., e111; label(a*b) = label(a) XOR label(b)

summary: An unintended extra gapless mode pinned at quasi-energy 0 or pi in a periodically driven quantum walk; in this project, the Floquet form of fermion doubling that Paper B's 3+1 walk designs must exclude or count exactly.
explanation: A quantum walk driven by a repeating cycle of steps has quasi-energies instead of ordinary energies: phases living on a circle, where 0 and pi (halfway around) are the two special self-symmetric points. When such a walk is engineered to imitate a single relativistic particle, the update rule can accidentally support additional massless modes sitting exactly at quasi-energy 0 or pi. These stowaways are aliases: momentum-space copies nobody asked for, much as a low video frame rate makes a fast wheel appear to spin slowly. In this project the term names the doubling symptom specific to driven walks; a mode at 0 or pi shows up as a root of the determinant of the one-step Bloch symbol at eigenvalue +1 or -1.
why: Whether a lattice automaton can host a single unpaired chiral fermion is the content of doubling no-go theorems, and in Floquet systems the pi modes are an extra channel with no static counterpart. For this program, Paper B's submission gate is exactly an alias-free 3+1 successor or the sharpest proved obstruction, so counting zero/pi aliases decides the paper.
example: The repo's exact even-parity alias theorem: every momentum-independent onsite coin in the live factorized 3+1 architecture leaves a zero/pi alias, kernel-checked (Paper B section of the publication portfolio).
conventions: Quasi-energy is measured on the circle (-pi, pi]. Aliases at quasi-energy 0 are detected by zeros of det(U(k) - 1) and at pi by zeros of det(U(k) + 1), where U(k) is the walk's Bloch symbol.
notation: modes at quasi-energy 0 or pi; det(U(k) -+ 1) = 0

summary: A minimal 1+1D picture of a massive particle: a massless left-mover repeatedly flipping into a massless right-mover, trapped in place by the flips; in this project the chirality-flip amplitude is kernel-proved equal to the Pluecker wedge of the two null directions.
explanation: A massless particle must move at light speed, so how can an electron sit still? The zigzag answer: at rest it is secretly two light-speed motions taking turns. A left-moving massless half flips into a right-moving one and back, over and over, and the rapid alternation averages to zero net motion. The flip rate is the mass: faster flipping means a heavier particle. The picture goes back to Feynman's checkerboard and Penrose's zigzag, and in the Standard Model the Higgs field is what licenses the flip between the two chirality halves. In this project the picture is upgraded from metaphor to machine-checked statement: in the minimal 1+1D model, the chirality-flip amplitude exactly equals the Pluecker wedge, the geometric disagreement between the two lightlike directions.
why: It reframes mass as trapped, disagreeing lightlike motion, which is the founding claim of the P1 origin-of-mass manuscript, and the flip-amplitude-equals-wedge identity is its central exact result. The later spiral-layer work sharpens the picture: zigzag (orientation-blind) content carries the mass magnitude, while oriented content carries phase, spin transport, and CP.
example: An electron at rest modeled as ...left, right, left, right... light-speed segments on a 1+1D lattice, with a flip amplitude per corner; the particle's mass is that amplitude, and switching the flip off leaves two free massless movers.
conventions: In this project zigzag content means the orientation-blind magnitude data of a path; the spiral-layer results prove it is CP-inert at all orders, with all CP-odd content living in oriented (Bargmann-phase) data. The checkerboard corner factor i is a theorem in-repo, not an input convention.
